doc_name: List of The Dukes of Hazzard episodes
text: This is a list of episodes for the 1979–1985 CBS action-adventure/comedy series The Dukes of Hazzard. The show aired for seven seasons and consisted of 147 episodes. Many episodes followed a consistent structure: "out-of-town crooks pull a robbery, Duke boys blamed, spend the rest of the hour clearing their names, the General Lee flies and the squad cars crash." Additionally, almost every episode began with the Duke boys driving in the General Lee, either running an errand or on a leisurely drive, and inadvertently stumbling upon one of the sheriff's speed traps. The Duke family resides in Hazzard County, Georgia. Their patriarch is Jesse Duke, a farmer and former moonshiner who is very wise and likely the most trusted person in six counties; his nephews, Bo and Luke, and his niece, Daisy, live on the Duke farm with him. Jesse raised Bo, Luke, and Daisy after their parents died in an auto accident. The family has made moonshine for generations. A few years prior, Bo and Luke were stopped on a moonshine run, and Jesse swallowed his pride to sign a treaty with the U.S. government to stop making moonshine if they could be released on probation. Since then, Jesse has honored his word and no longer runs moonshine. Despite being on probation, Bo and Luke continue to have fun, helping Jesse manage the farm and operating a souped-up orange Dodge Charger called the General Lee. Daisy works as a waitress at the Boar's Nest, the most popular bar/restaurant in the county, which is owned by the corrupt Hazzard County commissioner, Boss Jefferson Davis "J.D." Hogg. Boss Hogg owns nearly everything in Hazzard County, including bumbling Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane. Boss would do anything to make a dishonest dollar but does not condone violence. He plans to have Rosco receive a delivery of illegal slot machines, and Rosco is loyal enough to follow his orders. After about 20 years as one of the best lawmen in the state, most of Rosco's pension was lost in the last bond election in Hazzard County, making him bitter and corrupt. He is now running for re-election against an even more corrupt opponent. After hijacking the shipment of illegal slot machines, Bo and Luke plan to distribute them to civic clubs and organizations in the area and use the proceeds to help renovate the local orphanage before the health department shuts it down. Guest stars include Tisch Raye as Jill Rae Dodson; Ernie Brown as Dobro Doolan; Dan Fitzgerald as driver; Champ Laidler as Brodie; Gillaaron Houck as Leroy; Lou Walker as Workman; Dennis Haskins as Moss; Sandra Dorsey as Deputy Hazel; Ralph Pace as Harvey; Jason Lively as Rudy. Notes indicate that younger Dukes fans may recognize Dennis Haskins, who played Moss in this pilot episode, as he later became Mr. Belding on Saved by the Bell and had other recurring guest roles on The Dukes. Main characters Cooter Davenport (Ben Jones) and Deputy Enos Strate (Sonny Shroyer) do not appear in the opening credits and are only recognized in the end credits. In one episode, an Atlanta music-publishing outfit steals $50.00 from Daisy (a corruption of Boss Hogg's), and the FBI is monitoring the scam. Bo and Luke go to town to resolve the issue and end up interfering with a police raid. They devise a plan to catch the record pirates by having Daisy pretend to be a potential client to trick the music outfit's leader, Lester Starr, into believing she can fake recordings of real-life artists. Meanwhile, after being in the wrong place at the wrong time, Bo and Luke are targeted by the FBI and local law. Boss sees an opportunity to tie in with the syndicate, with a new singer Starr must audition for them and Boss, who just happens to be Daisy. This is a big mistake. Guest stars include Ronnie Schell as Lester Starr; Ginny Parker as Mabel; Clayton Landey as Max; Terry Browning as Ruby; Candy Bleick as Dodie; Wallace Merck as Jojo; Bill Gribble as Carson; J. Roy Tatum as FBI Agent #3; Wallace Wilkinson as FBI Agent #1; Bob Cleveland as FBI Agent #2. Notes state that while Bo and Luke discuss their plan in Atlanta, the sign of the first Mellow Mushroom pizza chain can be seen behind Bo. Loretta Lynn's name (as well as Coulter's) are dubbed over at several points in the episode. Bill Gribble, who appears as "Carson," also appeared in Moonrunners as Cooter Pettigrew. This episode marks the first time Cooter delivers his standard CB intro: "Breaker 1, breaker 1. I maybe crazy but I ain't dumb. Crrrrazy Cooter comin' at ya!" While fleeing from Enos in Cooter's car, Bo and Luke face a problem: the vehicle is loaded with moonshine that Cooter was supposed to deliver for Boss Hogg. Bo and Luke pick up a hitchhiker they recognize as their friend Mary Kaye Porter (Jeanne Wilson), who is now nine months pregnant and fleeing from Atlanta crime boss Quirt McQuade (Cliff Pellow), who believes Mary Kaye has $118,254.37 stolen from him. When McQuade tracks Mary Kaye to the Duke farm, where she gives birth to a girl, the Dukes use all their resources to protect Mary Kaye and her newborn. Guest stars include Jeanne Wilson as Mary Kaye Porter; Cliff Pellow as Quirt McQuade; Colby Chester as Leo. Boss Hogg plans to buy his wife Lulu, who is Rosco's sister, a Rolls-Royce from a car lot run by Ace Parker (Jerry Rushing), a crooked car dealer who has already sold the car to a counterfeiting ring. Boss and Ace want Bo and Luke to repossess the car so Lulu can have it. It is not easy, especially when Bo and Luke discover that Boss and Ace have been selling stolen cars and have set a trap to make it look like Bo and Luke stole them. The counterfeiters have hidden counterfeit $20 bill engraving plates in the car, so they are reluctant to give it up. Guest stars include Larry Bishop as Joey Sagalo; Judith Baldwin as Joey's Moll; Peggy Rea in her first appearance as Lulu Coltrane-Hogg; Rod Amateau as Manny; Claude Humphrey as Big John; Jerry Rushing as Ace Parker. Jesse decides to fire up his old moonshining still for a good cause—the Federal Energy Commission is seeking a clean fuel substitute for fossil fuels in a contest with a $20,000 prize, and the Dukes enter Jesse's famous moonshine recipe because it once powered Black Tillie, Jesse's old moonshining car. When Boss Hogg hears about the contest, he plans to steal Jesse's recipe to use in his own entry to win the money. Meanwhile, federal agent Roxanne Huntley (Charlene Watkins) arrives in town to investigate possible moonshine running. Guest stars include Carlene Watkins as Agent Roxanne Huntley; Champ Laidler as Brodie; Ralph Pace as Ed Monroe; Bob Hannah as The inventor. Swamp Molly (Neva Patterson), an old moonshining friend of Jesse's, wants to make "one last run" and asks the Dukes to help, as Molly saved Jesse from the Feds in the fall of 1936 and Jesse owes her. The Dukes do not know that Molly is no longer dealing moonshine—her truck is full of contraband firearms that could get Bo and Luke in trouble for violating their probation. Guest stars include Neva Patterson as Swamp Molly; Mary Jo Catlett as Cousin Alice; Bill Cort as Agent Callas. In the annual Hazzard County Obstacle Derby, Amy Creavy (Roz Kelly), from Placid County, becomes the first woman ever to enter. Luke is attracted to her, and they develop a relationship, but Luke struggles to accept that he cannot pursue other women if he and Amy are together. Things become dangerous when it is discovered that Amy's ex-boyfriend, her former mechanic Turk Foley (David Hayward), is determined to either get her back or kill her. Amy had fired Turk and replaced him with Francis Lee "Frankie" Olmstead (Marya Small) because Turk had put nitrous oxide in Amy's engine. Nitrous oxide increases a car's horsepower but can disqualify a driver. The Racing Association banned Turk as a driver for life after he severely injured four drivers. Boss Hogg wants to win the race because Mama Hogg's ashes are in the winning trophy, but honest deputy Enos Strate is driving for Boss, so Boss threatens Rosco to sell Cooter's truck unless Cooter becomes a crasher in the race to ensure Enos wins. Turk sabotages Amy's race car and then sneaks into the race using Cooter's car. The race ends between Luke, Amy, and Turk, and Amy and Luke do not know that Turk has taken Cooter's place. Guest stars include Roz Kelly as Amy Creavy; Marya Small as Francis Lee Olmstead; David Hayward as Turk Foley; Gary Grubbs as Roy; Patrick Wright as Moss. While Boss Hogg is counting his moonshine money, he is robbed of $30,000 by Neil Bishop (Fred McCarren), a chicken farmer that Boss knowingly sold defective farming equipment to. Neil stole the money to recover what he paid Boss for the equipment. Boss falsely accuses Bo of the robbery and tells Rosco. Neil ends up at the Duke farm after Daisy meets him at the Boar's Nest. When the Dukes learn about what Boss did to Neil, they decide to turn the tables by sending revenuer Harvey Essex (Stu Nisbet) after Boss. Guest stars include Fred McCarran as Neil Bishop; Stu Nisbet as Harvey Essex; Bill Meadows as the station attendant. President Jimmy Carter sends his car, "Limo One," to Georgia before visiting the state. The Secret Service and two state police motorcycle cops transporting the limo stop at the Boar's Nest for fuel and coffee, just as Cooter and the Duke boys are leaving. Bo and Luke spot the car, admire it, and leave. Cooter stays behind and becomes so fascinated by the limo that he hot-wires it and takes it for a joyride. Meanwhile, Boss Hogg operates a chop shop, and Rosco, who usually participates in Boss's scams, is unaware. When the limo goes missing, Rosco assumes the same car thieves who have been active in the county stole it. Boss realizes he has a disaster on his hands if his men at the chop shop cut the car up, until Rosco questions how much reward Boss would get for returning the "important car." Guest stars include Charles Cyphers as Bumper; Del Monroe as Benteen; Mayf Nutter as Dooley; Terry Willis as Tailor. After being in the wrong place at the wrong time, Bo and Luke are arrested and the General Lee is impounded. Crime boss Rocky Marlowe (Leo Gordon) is scheduled to be escorted from Springville to Hazzard County for trial. Boss sees a money-making opportunity with a high-profile trial and decides to send Bo and Luke to transport Marlowe from Springville in exchange for not selling the General Lee at police auction. Bo and Luke agree and leave, but not before being spotted in deputy uniforms by Daisy and Cooter. Along the way, they must deal with Herky (Bob Hoy) and Manny (Pat Renella), two of Marlowe's henchmen trying to free him. Traveling with Bo and Luke as a police officer is Mary Beth Malone (Stella Parton), who has a personal grudge against Marlowe and plans to kill him. Guest stars include Stella Parton as Mary Beth Malone; Leo Gordon as Rocky Marlowe; Norman Alden as Chief Lacey; Robert F. Hoy as Herky; Pat Renella as Manny; Suzanne Niles as Maybelle; Tara Preston as Cindy Lou; Billy Benedict as the gas station owner. Boss Hogg frames Bo and Luke for the robbery of $1 million in retired currency. He plans to bury the money in a coffin, report it stolen, receive an insurance check, and then unearth it. Guest stars include Rick Hurst as Cletus; Norman Bartold as company representative; Dan Barrows as attendant; Hoke Howell as watchman. To raise $180 to pay Cooter for General Lee repairs, Bo and Luke take a job driving an 18-wheeler for Helen Hogan (Joann Pflug), only to discover they are transporting a mobile casino. Jesse's old friend Dewey Stovall (Paul Brinegar) is gambling away his life savings in the casino. Boss wants to shut it down to take the equipment and start his own casino. To resolve the situation, the Dukes use their trump card—Jesse. Guest stars include Jo Ann Pflug as Helen Hogan; Theodore Wilson as Morgan; Paul Brinegar as Dewey Stovall. After fighting at the Boar's Nest against Tom Colt (Burton Gilliam), a stranger who tried to assault Daisy, Bo and Luke are arrested. At the jail, local physician Dr. Henry Petticord (Pat Cranshaw) suspects Colt has the plague and quarantines the jail with the police, Bo, Luke, and Jesse. Meanwhile, the Hazzard bank, owned by Boss Hogg, is robbed by Irving (Arte Johnson) and Wendel (Avery Schreiber), disguised as Laurel and Hardy, and Daisy chases them. Boss and Rosco falsely accuse Bo and Luke of setting up the robbery, which was actually Tom Colt's plan to get Boss, Rosco, and Enos out of the way while Irving and Wendel robbed the bank. The only way for Bo and Luke to clear their names is to escape the jail and go after Irving and Wendel, who have kidnapped Daisy. Guest stars include Arte Johnson as Irving; Avery Schreiber as Wendel; Burton Gilliam as Tom Colt; Joseph Burke as Sheriff Emmett "Hammerhand" Ragsdale; Pat Cranshaw as Dr. Henry Petticord. After seeing an old film of Boss Hogg and Jesse running moonshine, an argument over who is the better moonshine runner—prompted by Bo—leads Boss and Jesse to declare a race to determine the better runner. They agree to use jugs of water instead of moonshine, but Boss plans to win by switching the water in Jesse's car for moonshine, sending Jesse to Sheriff Emmitt "Spike" Loomis (Jim Mohlmann), known for being harsh on moonshiners. After discovering Boss's scheme, Bo, Luke, Cooter, and Daisy must alert Jesse of what he is carrying and switch the jugs back to water mid-race. Guest stars include Pat Buttram as Sam; Shug Fisher as Homer; Jim Mohlmann as Sheriff Emmitt "Spike" Loomis; Ancel Cook as Abel; Richard Marion as Helper #1. H. H. Harkness (Curtis Credel), a shady character from Texas, arrives in Hazzard and pays Boss Hogg $25,000 to store a pile of gold bars in the Hazzard Bank, claiming the gold is worth $3,000,000. When the gold is stolen, Bo and Luke are suspected. The Dukes discover the gold is actually lead painted to look like gold. Harkness is a swindler using the fake gold to try to defraud Boss of $3,000,000 in insurance money in the event of a robbery. Guest stars include Curtis Credel as H. H. Harkness; Bruce M. Fischer as Buck; Hunter von Leer as Dusty; Adam Wade as Dr. Homer Willis. Jesse's friend Burl Tolliver (Mel Tillis) plans to race his horse, Manassas, in the annual Lulu Hogg Stakes. Rosco sees Manassas in a time trial against the General Lee and reports it to Boss Hogg. Boss steals Manassas for his own use in the race, and then Manassas is stolen by Dunlap (Brett Halsey) and Cowan (Michael MacRae), who plan to sell it to a man from Nashville, Tennessee for $30,000. Guest stars include Peggy Rea as Lulu Coltrane Hogg; Mel Tillis as Burl Tolliver; Brett Halsey as Dunlap; Michael MacRae as Cowan; Dorothy Collier as Sherry Tolliver; Sam Edwards as Track Steward; Rick Hurst as Cletus Hogg.
