text: Fischer plays Buck; Hunter von Leer plays Dusty; Adam Wade plays Dr. Homer Willis. Jesse's friend Burl Tolliver (Mel Tillis) plans to race his horse, Manassas, in the annual Lulu Hogg Stakes race, but Rosco sees Manassas in a time trial against the General Lee and reports it to Boss Hogg. Boss steals Manassas for his own use in the race, and then Manassas is stolen by Dunlap (Brett Halsey) and Cowan (Michael MacRae), a pair of thieves who plan to sell him to a man from Nashville, Tennessee for $30,000. Guest starring: Peggy Rea as Lulu Coltrane Hogg; Mel Tillis as Burl Tolliver; Brett Halsey as Dunlap; Michael MacRae as Cowan; Dorothy Collier as Sherry Tolliver; Sam Edwards as Track Steward; Rick Hurst as Cletus Hogg. Boss Hogg's cousin Cletus Hogg, who is much more honest than Boss Hogg, is substituting for Enos, who is in the hospital with appendicitis. Boss Hogg buys $10,000 in stolen TV sets so he can sell them for a higher price, but Marty Garbade (Billy Green Bush), the man that Boss bought the TVs from, hijacks the truck that is delivering the TVs to Boss. The truck's driver makes a mistake in identifying the hijackers, getting Cletus and the Duke boys wrongfully accused of the hijacking. The Dukes set out to clear themselves and Cletus. While Bo and Luke are skinny dipping, the General Lee is stolen by Ernie (Caskey Swaim) and Phil (Russ McCubbin), a pair of pool hustlers who drive it into the Hazzard Pond while being chased by Rosco. Unaware that it was not Bo and Luke who were driving the car, Rosco thinks Bo and Luke drowned, and a grief-stricken Rosco tells that to Boss Hogg, Enos, Jesse, and Daisy. Boss schemes to take advantage of the situation by claiming that Bo and Luke stole his genuine Jefferson Davis gold watch and chain so he can collect the insurance on it. Bo and Luke find themselves arriving at their own wake. When they learn that Boss has accused them of stealing his gold watch and chain, they figure that the only way to prove their innocence is to haunt Boss and Rosco by making the General Lee look like a ghost, in order to scare the truth out of Boss. Ernie and Phil are in on the action, planning to rob Boss Hogg's safe at the Boar's Nest. Guest starring: Caskey Swaim as Ernie; Russ McCubbin as Phil; Norman Alden as Sheriff Lacey; Dixie K. Wade as Becky Mae's Mother; Debra Feuer as Becky Mae. While on the run after being framed by Boss and Rosco for crossing the county line and violating their probation, Bo and Luke discover that NASCAR driver Cale Yarborough (as himself) is testing a new turbo charger in preparation for the Illinois 500, and they bring Cale to Hazzard County to get his car serviced by Cooter. Boss Hogg gets in with Cale's biggest opponents, the Jethro brothers, Simon (William Watson) and Rowby (Tom McFadden), and helps them attempt to steal Cale's turbo charger, so the Jethro brothers can win the race. Guest starring: Cale Yarborough as himself; Harrison Page as Chet Garvey; William Watson as Simon Jethro; Tom McFadden as Rowby Jethro; Lindsay Bloom as Mabel Tillingham; Ray Guth as Amos Stigger; Joey Sagal as Motorcycle Guy (uncredited). Bo and Luke help Cooter deliver demolition derby cars to Augie Detweiller (John Quade), who runs a traveling demolition derby. Unbeknownst to Bo and Luke, Augie is smuggling stolen racing engines in the derby cars. Rosco discovers the smuggling, and he plans to arrest Bo and Luke. Bo and Luke decide to clear themselves by joining the derby, with Bo going undercover as a driver. Guest starring: John Quade as Augie Detweiller; Med Flory as Shoulders; Gerald McRaney as First workman. Boss Hogg is an important government witness against one of the biggest racketeers in the South, but the racketeer has assigned two hit men, Warren (L.Q. Jones) and Barnes (Bob Hastings), to stop Boss from testifying at the trial, which is scheduled to take place in Savannah. After Boss's life is threatened, an attorney named Tom Pryor (R. G. Armstrong) enlists the help of the Dukes in protecting Boss until it is time for him to testify. While Boss is hiding out at the Duke farm, Rosco takes over his administrative duties, wearing Boss's white continental suits, and relishing the job's absolute authority. Guest starring: R.G. Armstrong as Tom Pryor; L.Q. Jones as Warren. When counterfeit $5 bills start turning up, Bo and Luke try to figure out where the bills came from, and it turns out that the bills came from their old friend Granny Annie Coggins (Laurene Tuttle), a local artist who is operating a small-time counterfeiting scheme. Boss Hogg hears of it, and he wants the engraving plates that are used to make the bills, because he wants to sell the plates to professional counterfeiter Big Jim Downey (George Murdock) for $25,000. Boss has Granny Annie arrested, and confiscates the engraving plates. Bo and Luke set out to clear Granny Annie's name by stealing the plates back and throwing them into a lake. When Bo and Luke swipe the plates from Big Jim, Big Jim thinks that it is a double cross, so he kidnaps Boss, who he thinks is the one who stole the plates. An emotional Rosco pleads to Bo and Luke to track down Big Jim, and keep Boss from getting killed. Celebrity speed trap: The Oak Ridge Boys, who perform "Old Time Lovin'". Bo and Luke become campaign managers for Thelma Claire "T. C." Rogers (Pat Klous), who is running against Boss Hogg for the office of Supervisory Administrator of Hazzard County, a position that Boss cheated her father, Jim Rogers, out of 15 years ago. Boss tries every dirty trick he can think of in his efforts to stop T. C. from winning, let alone registering to run. Bo and Luke help T. C. in her efforts to counter Boss's dirty tricks. T. C. wins by one vote, proving that at least half of Hazzard County is not afraid to vote against Boss. Jesse is arrested for car-stripping when he is spotted at the scene of a car stripping incident by a motorist, while the real car strippers are a group of female mechanics who are working for Boss Hogg. Boss Hogg sells the parts back to the unsuspecting owners. Boss does not even want the temporary acting sheriff—his even more crooked nephew Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman)—to get in on the scam. Meanwhile, Rosco is out of town to take a refresher course at the Police Academy in Atlanta. Gaylord Duke (Simon MacCorkindale), the Dukes' cousin from London, England, comes to Hazzard to claim a piece of property that was willed to him, but the property has $30,000 in back taxes owed on it. Boss Hogg is planning to buy the property for almost nothing at an auction, and sell it to the Dixie King Supermarket chain for $250,000. Gaylord Duke turns out to be Roger Blevin, a con artist who left the real Gaylord Duke behind in England. The British Dukes' names are Philip and Katrina, and the real Gaylord is a preacher. Guest starring: Simon MacCorkindale as Gaylord Duke / Roger Blevin; Ernie Lively as Longstreet B. Davenport; Jim B. Smith as Tax Collector. Suzy Holmes (Susan Walden) is on the run from her snobby father, wealthy Tulsa, Oklahoma industrialist C. J. Holmes (Robert Alda), who has sent two private investigators named Les Sloane (Lance LeGault) and Mitch Henderson (Robert Tessier) to Hazzard to stop Suzy from marrying her fiancée Fred Andrews (Edward Edwards), just because Fred is a farmer. C. J. wants Suzy to marry someone within her social class, not someone involved in what C. J. sees as an unglamorous profession. C. J. will stop at nothing—even kidnapping Jesse. Jesse gives C. J. a stern lecture about the dedication and self-sacrifice of farmers. When C. J. finally comes to his senses, after Daisy's yellow 1971 Plymouth Road Runner plunges off of a cliff because of a jammed throttle, and explodes, C. J. is no longer against the marriage taking place. As an apology to Daisy for the destruction of her car, C. J. gives Daisy a new white 1980 Jeep CJ-7 called Dixie. Guest starring: Robert Alda. Boss Hogg buys an old tank to use in his J. D. Hogg War Memorial in front of the Boars Nest. Things get out of hand when the Dukes try to help old family friend Hard Luck Jones (Fred Stuthman) kick the habit of running moonshine, and Hard Luck swipes the tank to use as a rolling still. When Bo and Luke try to help Hard Luck, and the tank gets stuck on Duke property, it turns into a race to get rid of the tank before Boss Hogg and local ATF agent Buchanon (John Crawford) find them. As it turns out, Boss is using the tank as a storage place for contraband cigarettes. Guest starring: Fred Stuthman as Hard Luck Jones; John Crawford as Agent Buchanon; Ernie Lively as Longstreet B. Davenport; Ted Markland as Flint. College history professor Laura Bardsley (Jeannie Wilson) has arrived in Hazzard to find a buried Civil War strongbox that was buried before the Battle of Hazzard, and it contains a regimental payroll. Boss Hogg is also after the strongbox along with acting Hazzard County Sheriff Lester Crabb (Note: Rosco is still said to be in Atlanta at the police academy). Laura promises to give Boss Hogg and Sheriff Crabb the money contained in the strongbox, as long as she keeps the historic documents and other items of interest in it. Fortune hunter Stacy Williams (Doris Dowling) and her accomplice, Dr. James Fenwick (Whit Bissell), will stop at nothing to get to the strongbox first. The Dukes become involved, and help Laura recover the strongbox when it is stolen by Stacy and Dr. Fenwick. Guest starring: Jeannie Wilson as Professor Laura Bardsley; Doris Dowling as Stacy Williams; Whit Bissell as Dr. James Fenwick; Walter Barnes as Jeb McCobb; Cindy Acker as Sam McCobb; Sandy Acker as Gerry McCobb; Duke Robbins as Zack. Luke unintentionally gets Daisy fired from the Boar's Nest by helping her ask Boss Hogg for a raise. With Rosco still at the police academy in Atlanta, Boss hires a new temporary acting sheriff, Grady Byrd (Dick Sargent), who has been the night watchman at the Hazzard County Gravel Pit for 20 years. Boss Hogg tells Grady that the Dukes are the enemy, and to keep the Dukes out of his hair. Daisy cannot find another job, so Enos suggests that Daisy apply for a position as a Hazzard County deputy. Jesse is all for it, but Boss Hogg is against the idea of having any Duke work as a deputy. Enos spots Floyd Baker (Peter Brown) and Molly Harmon (Jenny Neumann), a pair of wanted bank robbers. Enos contacts Grady, who finds the robbers and chases them. Grady stops their car and takes them to the Hazzard jail. Later, Grady gives Daisy and two other female candidates a written and physical test. Daisy is the only one who passes, and as much as Boss Hogg and Grady hate it, they have no choice but to make Daisy a deputy. Bo and Luke get overprotective of Daisy, and Daisy makes it clear that she does not want any help from Bo and Luke. When Daisy gives Boss Hogg a ticket for parking in a red zone, Boss Hogg tells Grady to make sure Daisy does not patrol any more beats. Boss tells Grady to make Daisy do the kind of jobs that would make her quit her job as a deputy. Later, at the jail, Floyd and Molly knock Daisy out, and escape in her patrol car. Enos sees them leaving, but they get Enos off their tail. They even get Bo and Luke off their tail. Daisy comes to, and Boss, who wanted the $10,000 reward being offered to whoever gets Molly and Floyd, tells Grady to fire Daisy for letting Molly and Floyd escape. Grady fires Daisy, and outside, Bo and Luke want to go with Daisy to get Molly and Floyd, but Daisy tells Bo and Luke to stay out of the way, and then Jesse tells them to leave Daisy alone. Enos and Daisy go after Molly and Floyd, but Enos falls and hurts himself. Daisy takes his gun and continues after Molly and Floyd. When she finds them, they kidnap her and take her to an airfield, where their accomplice was waiting with an airplane. Bo and Luke arrive in the Jeep and collect Enos (who CB's the law). Then Bo and Luke shoot a dynamite arrow in front of the plane. In the commotion Daisy manages to get the gun from Floyd. Soon Grady and Boss arrive, and arrest Molly, Floyd, and their accomplice. Daisy is awarded a medal for bravery and the $10,000. Boss Hogg also hires her back as waitress at the Boar's Nest. Guest starring: Dick Sargent as Sheriff Grady Byrd; Peter Brown as Floyd Baker; Jenny Neumann as Molly Harmon; Jim Kindelon as Bartender; Rodney McGaughy as Driver; Nick Dimitri as Defense instructor (uncredited). When Loretta Lynn detours through Hazzard County, she is stopped by Boss Hogg's celebrity speed trap. Later, at the Boar's Nest, Loretta is kidnapped by Squirt (Henry Gibson), Bubba (Dennis Burkley), and Cindy (Rebecca Reynolds), the three members of an aspiring country music band who believe that Loretta is their key to success. They demand a ransom of $1,136.15 because they simply want to recoup the money that was cheated out of them by a fraudulent record label. Guest starring: Loretta Lynn as herself; Henry Gibson as Will "Squirt" Jason; Dennis Burkley as Bubba; Rebecca Reynolds as Cindy; Janet Meshad as Leona. Texas Ranger Jude Emery (John Shearin) has arrived in Hazzard in his search for dangerous crime boss Russel "The Snake" Harmon (Sam Melville), and Jude enlists the help of Bo and Luke in the search. Bo, Luke, and Jude are captured by Snake's gang, leading Daisy, Jesse, Cooter, and even acting Sheriff Grady Byrd to search for them. Guest starring: Dick Sargent as Sheriff Grady Byrd; John Shearin as Jude Emery; Sam Melville as Russel "Snake" Harmon; C. Pete Munro as Willie; George Buck Flower as Coy Randolph. Rosco returns from his refresher course at the Police Academy in Atlanta. Bo and Luke, thinking that there is a new hot water heater in the box that they picked up at the bus depot, soon discover that they have picked up a box full of marijuana, and Rosco arrests them. Private investigator Mason Dixon (Dennis Rucker) and his two associates, Tinker Churchill (Mary Margaret Humes) and Sam Rose (Robin G. Eisenmann), arrive in Hazzard to go after Dempsey (Morgan Woodward), the drug ring leader that the box of marijuana belongs to. Guest starring: Dennis Rucker as Mason Dixon; Mary Margaret Humes as Tinker Churchill; Robin G. Eisenmann as Samantha Rose; Taylor Lacher as Rayford Davis; Larry Watson as Johnny Ryan; Morgan Woodward as Dempsey; Lindsay Bloom as Mabel Tillingham. Henry Flatt (Hal Smith), a con artist who faked his death after swindling Boss out of $20,000 a year ago, shows up, and the Dukes try to help him with his problem: Boss Hogg is planning on plowing up an old veteran's cemetery to build a new highway and a subdivision called Hogg's Heavenly Acres—and plowing up that cemetery would alert Boss that Henry is still alive. Guest starring: Hal Smith as Henry Flatt; Audrey Landers as Gail Flatt; Jim English as Attendant. Jesse's cousin Holly Comfurt (Mariam Byrd Nethery) and her family suddenly strike it rich when Holly sells her farm for $250,000, but while in Hazzard, the Comfurts rent a Rolls-Royce that breaks down, and Cooter lends them a car while he fixes it. The loaner car is stolen from outside Cooter's garage by a drunk man, with the money in a case in the trunk, and then the car is sold to two men who plan to rob the Hazzard Bank, while Boss Hogg makes plans to get his hands on Holly's money. Guest starring: Miriam Byrd-Nethery as Holly Comfurt; Bernard Fox as Higgins; Edward Edwards as John Henry Comfurt; Lori Lethin as Lori Comfurt; John Lawrence as Frank Baldwin. When the Dukes go to see a stunt show called "The Carnival of Thrills", the star of the show, Bob Dexter (Richard Jensen), is injured while trying to jump a car over a pile of 32 cars, and that is the third consecutive time that that has happened in attempts to perform the 32-car jump. After that, the carnival's owner, Diane Benson (Robin Mattson), offers Bo a chance to use the General Lee to perform the 32-car jump. Bo falls for Diane, and agrees to do the jump. A feud erupts between Bo and Luke when Luke, fearing for Bo's safety, allows the General Lee to be impounded so Bo cannot do the stunt. What Luke does not know is that Boss Hogg plans to have the General Lee flattened and recycled so the Dukes cannot outrun Rosco anymore. And Boss Hogg also plans to take over the carnival by making sure Diane cannot pay the fee for using the Hazzard fairgrounds. After Luke and Bo learn that Boss plans to destroy the General Lee, the Dukes rescue the General Lee, but the situation leads to a fist fight between Bo and Luke. After the fight, Bo leaves the Duke farm, and prepares for the jump, but Luke, Daisy, and others are involved in the aftermath.

doc_name: List of The Dukes of Hazzard episodes
text: Bo attends a stunt show called "The Carnival of Thrills," where star Bob Dexter (Richard Jensen) is injured while attempting to jump a car over a pile of 32 cars for the third consecutive time. The carnival's owner, Diane Benson (Robin Mattson), offers Bo the chance to use the General Lee to perform the jump. Bo falls for Diane and agrees. A feud arises between Bo and Luke when Luke, fearing for Bo's safety, impounds the General Lee to prevent the stunt. Luke does not know that Boss Hogg plans to have the General Lee flattened and recycled so the Dukes cannot outrun Rosco, and also plans to take over the carnival by ensuring Diane cannot pay the fee for using the Hazzard fairgrounds. After learning of Boss's plans, the Dukes rescue the General Lee, leading to a fist fight between Bo and Luke. Bo leaves the Duke farm and prepares for the jump, but Luke, Daisy, and Jesse try to stop him. They receive shocking news from John Zimbra (Vernon Weddle), an insurance investigator, who reveals that the three previous 32-car jump attempts were not accidents—someone has been trying to kill drivers attempting the stunt, and Bo might be next unless Luke, Jesse, Daisy, and Cooter stop the saboteur. The saboteur is revealed to be Carl (Don Stroud), the carnival's former star performer who injured his knee and stopped driving, and who now sabotages jump attempts because he cannot stand being replaced. After Daisy takes a picture of Jesse in front of a bank in Atlanta, the Dukes notice the background shows a robbery with robbers removing their masks as they escape. The robbers follow the Dukes to Hazzard and kidnap Daisy, demanding the picture for her release. Enos—against Rosco's orders—helps rescue Daisy and is subsequently fired. Boss hires his cousin Cletus Hogg as deputy to replace Enos, who accepts a job with the Los Angeles Police Department and moves to Los Angeles. Rosco now has a basset hound named Flash. A pair of thieves, Claude Billings (Charles Tyner) and Billy Joe Billings (Andrew Robinson), steal Boss Hogg's silver collection from the Boar's Nest and hide it at an abandoned house inherited by Mary Lou Pringle (Morgan Brittany) from her uncle Ezekiah "Zeke" Pringle. Boss falsely believes Daisy, Bo, and Luke stole the silver. To keep Mary Lou away from the house, Claude and Billy Joe stage fake paranormal events to make it appear haunted, but Mary Lou has the Dukes on her side. A boxer named Catfish Lee (Sonny Shields) and his crooked promoter Billy Ray (Richard Schall) provoke Luke into a boxing match to profit from ticket sales. When Catfish knocks Luke into Boss Hogg's new $3,000 mirror at the Boar's Nest, Boss demands Luke fight Catfish to pay for the mirror, or Jesse must sell the Duke farm. Luke, a former boxer, reluctantly agrees, but Catfish, Billy Ray, and their boss Mr. Culpepper (Eddie Ryder) work to prevent Luke from reaching the match to keep all gate money. Boss Hogg successfully forecloses on the Duke farm and has the Dukes wrongfully arrested on a federal charge, but then learns from his doctor that he has a terminal illness with only two weeks to live. Believing that performing good deeds will save him from the devil, Boss gives the Dukes their farm back, drops the charge, and signs over many of his holdings to the poor people of Hazzard. Meanwhile, the Dukes must stop Linc McKay (James McIntire) and Dell Webber (Ray Young), who plan to rob the mail truck carrying $100,000 in Social Security checks and all the "good deed" papers Boss signed. The Dukes must retrieve the mail so the papers can reach their destination. Boss's doctor later reports that the diagnosis was incorrect and Boss is healthy. Boss is happy with the corrected results but devastated that the good deeds cannot be undone. Boss Hogg wants the Dukes out of his way permanently, so he calls his college-educated nephew Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) to Hazzard to eliminate them. Hughie frames Daisy for running moonshine, videotapes her escape with Bo and Luke, and takes the tape to Atlanta with Boss to turn it over to state police. Rosco, seeing the tape makes him look bad, tells the Dukes about Hughie's plan, and they all go to stop Hughie and Boss before they reach Atlanta. Boss Hogg's honest twin brother, Abraham Lincoln Hogg (Sorrell Booke), comes to Hazzard for the reading of their great-aunt Emma Lou Hogg's will, which entitles both brothers to land—but Boss had Abe declared legally dead five years ago when he disappeared in Africa. Abe has returned to claim his half of the land, but Boss has already sold it to a developer and arrests Abe in a nearby town to prevent him from attending the will reading. Luke and Daisy race to get Abe back before Boss secures the land for himself. After meeting Sue Ann Bliss (Tori Lysdahl) through a computer dating service, Rosco plans to marry and invites everyone in town except the Dukes to the wedding. The Dukes become the only possible suspects for the $100,000 miners' payroll robbery Boss arranges at the Hazzard Bank during the ceremony. Unknown to anyone, Sue Ann's real name is Sue Ann McGraw, and her husband Vic McGraw (Reid Smith) and friend Russ Collins (William Sanderson) are also planning to rob the bank. In the series' only Christmas-themed episode, Boss Hogg, in an Ebenezer Scrooge-like mood, hires Willie (Woody Strode), Russ (Brian Libby), and Hank (Roger Pancake) to hijack a truckload of Christmas trees that Bo and Luke are bringing to Hazzard for needy families and blame it on the Dukes. Russ and Hank steal the trees at gunpoint, Willie, disguised as a clergyman, gives Bo and Luke a lift into town and tells them they forgot their $500 down payment. With the town turning against the Dukes, they and Cooter race to find the trees and return Hazzard's Christmas spirit. Willie and his men plan to double-cross Boss by taking more than their payment and breaking into the Boar's Nest safe while dressed as Santa Claus. Bo and Luke, with Cooter's help, decide to take back the trees and deliver them to Hazzard dressed as Santa Claus, confusing Rosco and Cletus. The episode ends with forgiveness and fellowship as the Dukes and Cooter invite Rosco and Cletus to their Christmas Eve gathering. Boss arrives later, reformed after reading Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol. While being chased by Rosco, Bo and Luke crash on land believed to be unowned and discover they are wrong. They make friends with the new residents, the Bensons, who are actually federal witnesses Adam (John Larch) and Esther Venable (Cynthia Leake). Adam testified in a ransom case involving $2,000,000 in missing diamonds, and now the Venables are being chased by Hickey Burns (William Mims) and Leroy Little (Spencer Milligan), bounty hunters who believe Adam knows where the diamonds are. The Dukes must help the Venables avoid the hunters without getting killed. Boss Hogg mistakenly believes there is uranium in Hazzard. Daisy gives a stranger named Earl Beckett (Phillip Brown) a ride into Hazzard to work for Cooter, and Daisy begins to fall for Earl. The Dukes do not know that Hickman, the county commissioner in Claridge County (Larry D. Mann), has hired Earl to kill Boss so he can take over Boss's operations. Earl frames Bo and Luke for attempting to kill Boss. To clear their names, Bo and Luke must determine who Hickman hired. Lucinda Meadows (Jan Clayton), the first woman Jesse ever courted, returns to Hazzard to claim a $5,000 debt owed to her late husband by Boss Hogg. Boss refuses to pay. The Dukes find nine full barrels of moonshine in a mine under the Duke property. Lucinda plans to sell the moonshine to Boss Hogg, who intends to sell it to "mean" Joe Hatcher (Gregory Walcott). Hazzard's first annual Hazzard Derby takes place. Cooter borrowed money from Boss to build his car, which has a Cale Yarborough racing engine. If Cooter wins, the engine is sold and he receives a large sum. When Cooter is injured in a friendly race with Bo and Luke, Luke takes over driving. However, all entrants who signed contracts did not see the fine print stating that every loser must give up their car to Boss Hogg if Rosco wins. Boss believes Rosco's car cannot lose with a tank of nitrous oxide and places a $10,000 bet on Rosco with Chickasaw County bookie Ma Harper (Fran Ryan), who places a side bet on Rosco. Ma Harper tells her three sons to ensure Rosco wins. Chickasaw County moonshine dealer C. V. Gumble (Anne Haney) has customers demanding moonshine but lacks inventory. She calls Boss Hogg and offers to pay up to 10 times the going rate for a shipment, but Boss struggles to find a driver who is not afraid of Chickasaw County Sheriff "Big Ed" Little (Don Pedro Colley). Bo is driving a car he borrowed from Cooter on his way to meet a friend for a boar-hunting trip when Boss and Rosco chase him. Due to fallen boulders, Bo pulls off the road, gets out of the car, trips, and hits his head on a log. Boss and Rosco take Bo to the emergency room without telling the Dukes. When told Bo has amnesia, Boss sees a solution: he introduces himself as Bo's father and Rosco as Bo's uncle. Boss plans to get Bo to drive the moonshine into Chickasaw County. When Jesse, Luke, and Daisy figure out Boss's plan, they must get to Bo before Sheriff Little does. Myrna Roby (Martha Smith) and Burt Roby (James Crittenden), a couple who robbed a jewelry store in Nashville, come through Hazzard and are immediately arrested by Rosco on a false charge. When Boss and Rosco learn who the Robys are, they escape and hijack Bo and Luke in the General Lee. Boss now believes Bo and Luke were in on the robbery. Things become complicated when Rosco's dog, Flash, retrieves the stolen loot and takes it to Rosco's patrol car. Upset that he was not told about the stolen jewels (so he could take a cut), Boss fires Rosco. The Dukes must clear Bo and Luke's names. The Dukes receive a visit from their motorcycle-riding cousin Jeb Stuart Duke (Christopher Hensel), who lives in Claridge County. Atlanta museum curator Eustice Hastings (Earl Boen) has Bo and Luke transport General Stonewall Jackson's personal sword to Boss Hogg's annual Stonewall Jackson Day, but Boss plans to sell the sword for $25,000 to Beauregard Mason (Kenneth O'Brien), Georgia's biggest fencer of stolen goods. Boss hires thieves Vic (Michael Greene) and Corey (Alex Kubik) to steal tractors and other heavy equipment from farmers he previously loaned money to. Boss loaned them the money seven years ago when interest rates were low. Now that rates are higher, Boss feels he is losing about 15% annually. He has the equipment stolen and brought to him to recoup losses and plans to sell it to a buyer he has arranged. While Daisy moonlights as a contributing reporter at the Hazzard Gazette, Boss frames Bo and Luke for the thefts by having Vic and Corey set up the crime so Daisy's photograph shows Bo and Luke instead of the real thieves. Boss does not intend to jail Bo and Luke immediately—he wants them free long enough for Vic and Corey to complete the thefts. Daisy's editor, Clyde Amos (Richard Paul), wants the story regardless of who is in the photo. Daisy and Jesse beg Clyde not to have Bo and Luke jailed for something they did not do. Clyde tells the Dukes that the best he can do is give them eight hours until press time to find Vic and Corey so Bo and Luke can clear their names. Boss Hogg calls his nephew Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) back.

doc_name: List of The Dukes of Hazzard episodes
text: Boss Hogg plans to recover losses by stealing equipment from farmers and selling it to a buyer he has arranged with. While Daisy moonlights as a reporter at the Hazzard Gazette, Boss frames Bo and Luke for the thefts by having Vic and Corey set up a situation where Daisy’s photograph shows Bo and Luke instead of them. Boss does not intend to jail Bo and Luke immediately, only wanting them free long enough for Vic and Corey to complete the thefts. Daisy’s boss, editor Clyde Amos (Richard Paul), wants the story regardless of who is in the photo, and Daisy and Jesse plead with him not to have Bo and Luke jailed for something they did not do. Clyde agrees to give the Dukes eight hours before press time to find Vic and Corey so they can clear their names. Boss calls his nephew Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) back to Hazzard to eliminate the Dukes. Hughie convinces Bo and Luke to join the Hazzard County Fire Department so he and his henchmen, Barclay (Pat Studstill) and Norris (Roger Torrey), can sneak moonshine to the Duke farm during a fake fire call and frame Bo and Luke for possession. Hughie also swindles Boss out of all his possessions by having a fake IRS agent (John H. Fields) audit Boss. Now the Dukes and Boss must team up to take Hazzard back from Hughie, while Rosco’s sister and Lulu’s sister-in-law, Hortense Coltrane (Frances Bay), is visiting. On the way to the Boar’s Nest, Bo and Luke are ambushed by escaped convict Digger Jackson (Charles Napier), who steals the General Lee and plans to hunt down Boss Hogg, the man who imprisoned him 10 years ago. Bo and Luke are falsely accused of a robbery committed by Jackson, and when Jackson kidnaps Boss for ransom, no one in Hazzard wants to help retrieve him. The Dukes take on the task. Bo and Luke find a stack of money floating in Hazzard Creek, just a fraction of the $1,000,000 stolen in a highjacking five years earlier. Soon after, Luke’s Marine friend Phill Ackley (Rick Hill) arrives with his sister Kate (Simone Griffeth) and friend Tommy Dunkirk (Sam Melville); Phill claims Kate was wrongly blamed for the highjacking, and if the Dukes help recover the rest of the money, they can clear her name. However, Kate is actually Phill’s wife, and all three are responsible for the highjacking. To help family friend Emma Tisdale (Nedra Volz), Bo and Luke take over her taxicab service while Daisy and Jesse run the post office. Their first clients are J. J. Sunday (Peter Breck) and Harry Ray Pearson (Royce D. Applegate), who steal a $100,000 gold certificate. When Rosco approaches the taxi, the crooks hide the certificate in the backseat. Later, Cooter sends the seat for re-upholstery, finds the certificate, and mails it. The crooks now target Daisy, who is transporting outgoing mail. After buying a vase at Emma Partridge’s (Elizabeth Kerr) yard sale, where Emma hopes to pay off her mortgage to Boss Hogg, the Dukes are harassed by Mr. Beckman (Byron Webster), a major buyer, because the vase is worth a fortune. Mr. Beckman will do anything to get it, and Boss Hogg tries to cut in on the deal after learning Mr. Beckman is willing to pay $50,000. Starting with "Goodbye, General Lee," Warner Bros. begins producing "General Lee" chargers with light tan interiors, a wide push bar, and more consistent appearances. When Boss’s rich, polite nephew Jamie Lee Hogg (Jonathan Frakes), son of Boss’s youngest brother, comes to buy the grits mill, Daisy and Jamie fall in love quickly, and they plan to elope. However, because Jamie Lee’s last name is Hogg, Bo and Luke investigate and discover he is working with counterfeiter Roy Landry (Roger Robinson). Daisy has already left to meet him at the mill, so Bo and Luke must rescue her from Jamie Lee and the counterfeiters. Boss hires Turk (Robin Strand) and Moody (Morgan Stoddard), who use fake General Lee and masks to rob an armored car of $250,000, framing Bo and Luke. To clear their names, Bo and Luke must capture Turk and Moody, but Sheriff Little (Don Pedro Colley) joins the investigation. Bo and Luke find a bag of diamonds hidden in a stuffed Bugs Bunny doll parachuted from a hijacked airplane, and they take it to the Duke farm for safekeeping. Lisa (Linda Hart), the leader of the thieves, follows them to the farm, claiming to be a reporter to get the diamonds. Boss hears a reward is offered and sends a fake FBI agent, Mason (Joseph Whipp), to the farm to seize the diamonds under the pretense of a warrant. A beer distributor offers Boss top dollar for the Duke farm. After Bo and Luke accidentally run Rosco off the road, Boss forms a plan to have Rosco fake an injury and file a $50,000 personal injury lawsuit against the Dukes to win the farm. Boss hires actor Slick Doggins (Bob Hastings) to play a doctor to support Rosco’s claims. In reality, Rosco plays the victim so thoroughly that Boss is forced to serve him. When the Dukes prove Rosco is faking his injuries, they must deliver the evidence to Judge Buford Potts (Barney Phillips) before losing the farm. As the Dukes help Bo prepare for the Tri-Counties Motocross race, attractive drifter Mindy Lou Hale (Laurette Spang) overhears Boss and Rosco discussing stealing motorcycles from competitors, repainting them, and selling them to Leroy Dibbs (G. Yon). Boss wants Mindy Lou removed, so he orders Rosco to arrest her, but she escapes and is found by the Dukes, who try to help her. Boss, unwilling to pay longtime Hazzard Bank employee Clarence Stovall (Bill Erwin) his $30,000 pension, fires him one day short of retirement. Clarence decides to take the $30,000 from the bank, which is owned by Boss. Jesse, a friend of Clarence, learns about it and tries to help, while Bo and Luke, knowing Boss will arrest Clarence with Rosco, try to return the money without being caught. Boss is nervous when state bank examiner L. S. Handley (John Hancock) comes to inspect the county ledger, as he has embezzled exactly $142,679. Fortunately, it is Sadie Hogg Day, when women occupy government positions, so Boss arranges for Daisy to become the honorary county treasurer, framing her for the embezzlement. The Dukes must expose Boss’s cover-up before Daisy ends up in jail. Rosco inherits $10,000,000 from his great-uncle Hosiah Coltrane, but before receiving the money, he spends it lavishly: buying a Rolls-Royce patrol car, gaudy rhinestone suits, and speaking freely to Boss. Frustrated by years of being outsmarted, Rosco offers Jason Steele (William Smith), the meanest bounty hunter in Georgia, $100,000 to track down Bo and Luke and have them imprisoned. Steele and his partner Dawson (Alan Autry) arrive and pursue the Dukes. As Bo and Luke repeatedly escape Steele, Rosco swindles Boss out of everything he owns when Boss’s crooked poker game fails. Jesse learns Steele has a prior legal issue, and while trying to track him down, Jesse falls down a hill and hits his head, going into a coma. Rosco, feeling guilty, starts to question his plan, but Steele, wanting to protect his reputation, insists on continuing. Steele tricks Bo and Luke into driving a stolen Dodge Charger painted exactly like the General Lee, arresting them. It turns out Rosco’s inheritance is only $10 due to a computer error that misplaced the decimal. Boss regains all he lost and returns to being County Commissioner. Rosco is now in trouble with Steele, who wants the $100,000 he believes Rosco owes him, and Steele is trying to take Bo and Luke to Atlanta to face a car-theft charge. When Rosco says he cannot pay, Steele loses control, releases Bo and Luke without using a car, and kidnaps Rosco, hoping Boss will pay $100,000. Boss refuses, not realizing what is happening, because of how Rosco treated him. When Cooter gets the General Lee to Bo and Luke, they chase Steele and Dawson, while Jesse recovers. A pair of fur thieves, Russ Mitchell (Steve Sandor) and Bonnie Lane (Colleen Camp), come to Hazzard to sell Boss stolen mink coats. Boss shortchanges them by the price of a lost coat. Mitchell plans to break into the storage room at Boss’s place by going through a hole in the wall at Cooter’s Garage, while Bonnie distracts Cooter. Boss Hogg wants to win the first annual Hazzard County Drag 'n' Fly Derby to gain endorsements, but the only obstacle is the General Lee. After Luke loses a race and makes a comment about the General Lee possibly wearing out, Boss hears it. After Luke is injured during a qualifying jump, Boss hires Professor Crandall (Walker Edmiston) to hypnotize Luke into believing the General Lee is no longer roadworthy. To speed up the process, Boss orders Rosco to sabotage the General Lee by damaging its fuel line, causing another breakdown. After the car malfunctions, Luke, under hypnosis, decides to take it to a used car dealership to trade it, which upsets the Duke family. Bo, Daisy, and Jesse do not want to get rid of the General Lee, as it is part of the family. Boss buys the General from the dealership and arranges for it to be demolished. Cooter notices the unmanned General Lee coasting toward a cliff during a call and saves it with his tow truck. Luke even tries to blow it up with dynamite. When arguing with Bo, Jesse, and Daisy, Luke hears Jesse snap his fingers (the sound used by Professor Crandall to break the hypnosis), and Luke immediately changes his mind about the General Lee. Bo and Luke rush to reclaim the General Lee, then enter it in the derby and win, infuriating Boss Hogg. The first episode where viewers see the WB-built General Lees with wider push bars, light tan interiors, and graphics updates. Cletus initiates a traffic stop with the Dukes. When Daisy uses her charm to get Bo and Luke out of a fake ticket, Cletus thinks she is in love with him. Daisy tries to end the relationship without hurting him. Boss is upset when the state probation supervisor comes to Hazzard to evaluate his work. To impress the supervisor and keep his large paycheck as probation officer, Boss frames Bo and Luke for passing a bad check, requiring them to clear their names. Boss fires Cletus after he makes a bad arrest, prompting Cletus to side with the Dukes. To ensure the plan works, Boss brings in Chickasaw County Sheriff "Big Ed" Little to guard jailed Bo and Luke until they can be taken to the supervisor. Daisy eventually tells Cletus she is not in love with him (Cletus accepts it and begins dating another woman), and Bo and Luke get help from Flash, who clears them by eating Boss’s forged check. Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) sneaks back into Hazzard and convinces Boss not to kick him out of town for what he did a year ago. This time, Hughie has a scheme too good for Boss to refuse: for $25,000, he plans to frame.

doc_name: List of The Dukes of Hazzard episodes
text: Boss Hogg continues to receive a large paycheck as the Hazzard County probation officer by framing Bo and Luke for passing a bad check, forcing them to clear their names. After firing Cletus for bungling an arrest, Cletus aligns with the Dukes to help them. To ensure his scheme works, Boss brings in Chickasaw County Sheriff "Big Ed" Little to guard jailed Bo and Luke until they can be taken to the state probation supervisor. Daisy eventually tells Cletus she is not in love with him, and he accepts it, beginning a relationship with another woman. Bo and Luke receive unexpected help from Flash, who clears their names by eating Boss Hogg's forged check. Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) sneaks back into Hazzard County and convinces Boss not to kick him out, proposing a scheme for $25,000 to frame Cooter for robbery so Boss can use eminent domain to foreclose on Cooter's garage and build "Hoggominiums." Boss attempts to seize the Duke farm by faking a bank robbery with Rosco, who then locks Boss up; out of friendship and debt, Jesse bails Boss out, using the Duke farm as bail. If Boss jumps bail, the farm is forfeited to Boss Hogg himself. Boss does jump bail, but ends up locked in the bank's vault with Jesse for only one hour of air. Bo and Luke must escape and convince Boss to end the scam, searching for bank employee Emery Potter (Charlie Dell), the only person besides Boss who knows the vault combination. Boss is excited about the Mickey Gilley charity concert at Hazzard Square not for the music, but for the money. He works with Heep (Burton Gilliam) and Morton (L. Q. Jones), recording pirates, who steal the concert and sell it. When fleeing federal agents Marjorie Dane (Elinor Donahue) and Ben Jordan (Hari Rhodes), Heep and Morton hijack Bo and Luke in the General Lee. Bo and Luke fight them off, unaware that they left a concert tape in the backseat, which Boss uses to frame them. The Dukes capture Heep and Morton to clear Bo and Luke's names. Boss later tricks Mickey into performing at the Boar's Nest with his celebrity speed trap. Boss wants Jesse's moonshine recipe to sell to Jasper Fenwick (Jim B. Baker), the largest moonshine distributor in Georgia. When Jesse refuses, Boss hires a crooked magician to frame Bo and Luke for stealing money meant for an orphanage, then asks Jesse for the recipe in exchange for Bo and Luke's release. When the State Highway Commission gives Boss $10,000 for radar guns, he buys hair driers disguised as radar guns to pocket the money. Jesse's old friend Hector Farley (Henry Jones), returning after 10 years in prison, seeks to recover the farm Boss stole from him. Boss uses every dirty trick to send Hector back to prison while also framing Bo and Luke for destroying county property using Rosco's fake radar gun. Boss runs a scam through the mail selling non-existent properties, and when postal inspector Sue Ann Blake (Diane Lander) arrives, he frames postmaster Emma Tisdale (Nedra Volz). The Dukes hide Emma while trying to clear her name, but end up on the run. Emma falls for Jesse. Boss operates a crooked casino; when a state gambling probe begins, he frames the Dukes for possessing gambling devices. While at a police convention in Atlanta, Rosco collects a truth serum syringe, which Boss accidentally sits on and injects himself with, causing him to reveal too much about the casino. The Dukes must act before his partners silence him permanently. Under the serum, Boss reveals the real reasons he married Lulu, angering her. Rosco loses his diary on the Duke farm, filled with notes on every scam he and Boss have pulled. Jesse tries to deliver it to Boss and Rosco, but Hadley (Bill McLaughlin) and Avery (Ernie Hudson) steal it and demand $25,000 or turn it in to authorities. Boss plans to use Bo and Luke to retrieve the diary by blackmailing them with a book of trumped-up charges against the Dukes. The diary is destroyed in a car crash, and Boss's 20-year collection of charges is shredded in a woodchipper. A shapely, cajoling blonde named Linda May Barnes (Tracy Scoggins) is hired as Boss's deputy after easily arresting Bo and Luke on traffic charges. Her boyfriend, Rafe Logan (Terence Knox), is scheduled to stay overnight at the jail, and she and his brother Denny (Gary Graham) plan to free him from marshal Rayford Barnes (Rayford Barnes). Bo and Luke try to stop Linda May and Denny from helping Rafe escape. Daisy is offered a job racing on the NASCAR circuit by Molly Hargrove (Andra Akers), after Daisy beats Bo and Luke in a race through the woods. Molly has a loan from Boss, who hires crooks to ensure she cannot pay it off, forcing her to give Daisy's contract to Boss. Molly was expelled from NASCAR for reckless driving and wants Daisy to win at all costs. Bo, Luke, and Jesse must help Daisy. A group of armed robbers led by Mr. Thackery (Tim O'Connor) take over the Boar's Nest, holding the Dukes, Rosco, Cletus, Cooter, and Boss as hostages to rob an armored truck carrying $10,000,000. Thackery soon realizes capturing a Duke is easier than holding one. The annual Miss Tri-Counties pageant includes beauty, racing, and mechanical ability. One of Daisy's opponents is Melanie Dubois (Danone Simpson), the girlfriend of Big Jim Mathers (Joe Higgins), who pays Boss $10,000 to ensure Melanie wins. Boss rigs the racing and mechanical parts, but Daisy wins both. Daisy wants to participate in the swimsuit competition, which Boss tries to stop, but she makes it and wins. Bo and Luke find a bag of stolen credit cards hidden by Dickens (David Hayward) and Clark (Billy Ray Sharkey). Boss plans to sell the cards and frame the Dukes. Lulu forms the Hazzard Equal Rights Society (HERS) to assert women's rights, and Daisy joins. Lulu attempts to take over half of Boss's business, including his used car lot, and sells a car to Sheriff Little, unaware Boss hid the stolen credit cards in a door panel. Rosco and Cletus go on strike after being denied a pay raise and overtime, with Jesse appointed acting sheriff. Boss hires crooks led by Alabama Jones (Melinda Naud) to steal TV sets, framing Bo and Luke. When Jesse discovers the scheme, he helps Bo and Luke pursue the crooks. Two convicts, Leeman (Steven Williams) and Hammer (Bill Fletcher), escape from a prison car and go to the Duke farm, where Jesse is making a mortgage payment to Boss. They take the Dukes hostage, confiscate their car keys, and disable their communication devices. Boss and Rosco go to the farm to collect the payment and become hostages too. Everyone must cooperate to get Cooter and Cletus to rescue them. Bo and Luke leave Hazzard to race on the NASCAR circuit, and Boss is thrilled, unleashing his ultimate weapon—the Mean Green Machine. This vehicle is part of a plan to rob the Bank of Capitol City, which is only a test run. Boss and two men, Josh Scroggins (William Russ) and Hatfield (Mitch Carter), have a money printing press and the right paper, needing engraving plates from an armored truck with U.S. Mint plates. Boss plans to use the Mean Green Machine to hijack the truck and steal the plates. Unaware, Bo and Luke's cousins Coy and Vance return after six years to help Jesse and Daisy run the farm. Enos returns from Los Angeles and is sworn in as deputy by Rosco, giving Rosco two deputies: Cletus and Enos. Boss swindles newlyweds Jeb (Jay W. Baker) and Carrie Morton (Phyllis Hall) into buying worthless land next to the Duke farm, and the Dukes scam Boss by making it appear they found gold, so he buys it back. Boss hires demolition experts Jack Morris (Duke Stroud) and Burnett (Al White) to rob the Hazzard jewelry store, with Coy and Vance checking in while being chased by Cletus and Enos. When Boss sends Rosco to arrest them, Rosco refuses because he has nominated himself for "Lawman of the Year." Enos and Cletus are both elected. Coy and Vance drive antiques to Loomis for friends moving away, but are hijacked and robbed by Clooney (George McDaniel) and Potter (Robert Gray), with teenage runaway Bobbie Lee Jordan (Michelle Greene) stowing away and witnessing the robbery. Clooney and Potter plan to silence Bobbie Lee, who ends up at the farm and develops a crush on Coy. Sharkey (Earl Montgomery), Hopkins (F. William Parker), and Bowman (William Bramley), corrupt county commissioners, want Boss to pay for refusing to share highway profits and plan to take over Hazzard County. The Dukes team up with Boss to save Hazzard, letting him hide at the farm while Coy and Vance tape-record a conversation between them to expose them. Boss frames Coy and Vance by putting a stolen license plate on the General Lee. He calls off the chase when his father, Big Daddy Hogg (Les Tremayne), arrives in Hazzard, and after arriving, Big Daddy's driver robs Boss's safe at City Hall. Vance's former girlfriend Jenny Walden (Beth Schaffel) comes to Hazzard to see Vance, and is pursued by Wade (Gary Grubbs) and Dugan (Taylor Lacher), associates of corrupt State Senator Jason W. Maynard (Kirk Scott), who want to kill her for witnessing embezzlement. The Dukes try to convince Jenny to report Maynard to the Senate Crime Commission, but when Wade and Dugan trick Boss into helping them find Jenny, the Dukes face a difficult challenge. Boss opens a crooked horse-betting saloon in Rapaho County and uses the Duke family's phone line to frame them. In this episode, the General Lee has a distinct "01" on the passenger side door.

doc_name: List of The Dukes of Hazzard episodes
text: Big Daddy Hogg (Les Tremayne) has his driver rob Boss Hogg's safe at City Hall. Vance's former girlfriend Jenny Walden (Beth Schaffel) comes to Hazzard to see Vance, and she is being chased by Wade (Gary Grubbs) and Dugan (Taylor Lacher), associates of crooked State Senator Jason W. Maynard (Kirk Scott), who are trying to kill her because she witnessed Senator Maynard embezzling state funds. The Dukes try to convince a terrified Jenny to report Maynard to the Senate Crime Commission, but when Wade and Dugan trick Boss into helping them find Jenny, it will be too much for the Dukes to handle. Boss Hogg opens up a crooked horse-betting saloon in Rapaho County and, to cover his actions, uses the Duke family's phone line to frame the Dukes for it. Big Billie Tucker (Joy Garrett), the commissioner of Rapaho County, threatens to have Bull (Bruce M. Fischer), her muscle-bound henchman, kill Boss if he does not include her in the scam. The Dukes must now outmaneuver Tucker and Bull and outsmart Boss. Enos' footlocker is shipped back to Hazzard from Los Angeles, and Enos and the Dukes pick it up at the depot, not knowing that crooks Carter (Brett Halsey) and Burke (Anthony Eisley) have hidden a fortune in stolen emeralds inside Enos' flashlight, where its batteries are supposed to be. Carter and Burke are in Hazzard to get the emeralds, and Boss Hogg hears about them and also wants them. Boss Hogg's new insurance fraud scam is threatened when con artist Ward S. Davis (Brian Libby) and his girlfriend Lavinia Grey (Melanie Vincz) pull a phony car accident at Bottomless Lake after buying a $1,000,000 policy from Boss Hogg. Lavinia wants Boss Hogg to give them the $1,000,000. Coy is afraid of driving anymore because he was sideswiped during the fake accident and believes he killed Ward. Vance sets out to figure out what really happened, but ends up kidnapped. Can Coy overcome his fear of driving in time to help the rest of the Dukes find Ward and Lavinia and rescue Vance? The 37th annual Tri-Counties Amateur Pool Championship at the Boar's Nest is coming up, and Jesse is one of the competitors. Boss Hogg wants to get his hands on the General Lee so he can sell it to Joe Landis (Frank Pendle) and Don Purcell (Jesse D. Goins), a pair of hijackers who need a good getaway car. Landis and Purcell have compiled a list of every payroll shipment in the state, and Boss Hogg's plan is for them to hijack the shipments and split the money with Boss Hogg. When Landis and Purcell try to steal the General Lee, they are stopped by the Dukes, so Boss Hogg challenges Jesse to a game of pool—Ridge Runner style—and tricks Jesse into wagering the General Lee. Jesse is a better pool player than Boss, but Boss has dirty tricks, such as naming Chickasaw Thins (Robert V. Barron) as Jesse's opponent, because no one has ever beaten Chickasaw Thins. Jesse loses the General in the game, and now the Dukes have to find the General and get it back from Landis and Purcell, who have painted the General Lee black. Boss Hogg frames Coy, Vance, and Daisy for the theft of his gold cufflinks, has them arrested by Chickasaw County Sheriff Ed Little, and makes Enos busy with tasks that do not need to be done. Boss wants Enos and the Dukes out of the way so Biff Gregory (John Laughlin) and his accomplice Pruitt (Andrew Robinson), two men Boss made a deal with, can go ahead with their plan to search Soggy Marsh for $500,000 that a man named Kingston robbed from a bank 10 years ago. Instead of keeping them away, Boss's efforts spur the Dukes to escape and investigate. When Daisy finds Gregory and Pruitt first, she is kidnapped, and it is up to Coy, Vance, and Jesse to rescue her. Rosco is up for re-election, and Boss Hogg has no problem supporting him—until Boss Hogg's nephew Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) returns to Hazzard to run against Rosco for sheriff. Hughie blackmails Boss into helping him by showing Boss evidence of a crooked deal involving more than $10,000 worth of stolen telephone answering machines—the man who stole them wants Boss to fence them. Knowing Hughie would be worse than Rosco, the Dukes campaign to get Rosco re-elected. However, since Hughie never plays fair, he has Boss suspend Rosco and try to arrest the Dukes. The Dukes must get creative to outsmart Hughie, get Boss back on Rosco's side, and stop Hughie from being elected. Boss Hogg plans to use the Mean Green Machine to steal the $1,000,000 Jefferson Davis gold coin collection from the Hazzard Gold and Silver Emporium, but the Machine is stolen from Boss Hogg's henchmen by Baxter (Joel Bailey) and Hatfield (Mitch Carter), a pair of crooks who plan to use it to steal the gold coin collection themselves. Coy and Vance take on the Machine and manage to damage it. Baxter and Hatfield need a mechanic to fix it, so they kidnap Cooter and hold him hostage. Coy and Vance recognize Hatfield as one of the men who originally drove the Machine for Boss Hogg a few months ago—Hatfield and Baxter escaped from prison and are now after the gold coin collection. Floyd Calloway (R. G. Armstrong) has hired Matt Mallory (Rick Hill) and Lorna Mallory (Barbara Horan) to kill Boss Hogg because 20 years ago, Boss and Calloway were running moonshine together, and when federal agents started closing in, Boss turned state's evidence against Calloway to avoid prosecution. Feeling that Boss is in danger, the Dukes help Boss and plan to make Calloway think Boss is dead, so Calloway and the Mallorys will leave Boss alone. A pair of crooks have been disguising as motorcycle cops and robbing drivers on the roads. Vance suspects the robbers are Coy's new girlfriend, motorcycle stuntwoman Billie Ann Baxley (Shawn Weatherly), and her sister Kate Baxley (Bobbie Ferguson), but Coy refuses to believe Vance. This leads to a fight between Coy and Vance, causing Coy to leave the farm. Can Vance convince Coy of the truth? A Russian gymnastics team passing through Hazzard stops at Cooter's garage to get their bus serviced. The team's star gymnast, Natasha (Dawn Jeffory), escapes and hides in the bed of Jesse's pickup truck, hoping to reach Detroit, Michigan, where she has relatives. A group of KGB officials and their leader, Borov (Hank Garrett), were on the bus to prevent defection. The Dukes find Natasha in the truck and decide to help her escape from Borov, who will stop at nothing to find her and even seeks the help of Boss Hogg. Boss Hogg is trying to buy gas pumps from a crook named Hanson (Noble Willingham)—pumps that would overcharge gas buyers at Boss Hogg's stations. Jesse is blinded by a blow to the face while trying to stop a bank robbery in Capitol City, and his eyesight might not return. The robbers, Parker (Judson Scott) and his accomplice Rick (Billy Streater), do not want witnesses, so they go to Hazzard County to track Jesse down, planning to kill him. Coy, Vance, and Daisy decide to hide Jesse at Boss Hogg's house while they try to stop Parker and Rick. Bo and Luke return to Hazzard County after a great season on the NASCAR circuit, where they won in Mobile, Alabama (in storyline; in actuality, the track is in Irvington, where it was the home of NASCAR's Grand American and regional series). They wanted to come home because they missed Hazzard County too much to stay away. Coy and Vance have decided to leave Hazzard to take care of their Uncle Elbert and Aunt Bessie's farm while Elbert is in the hospital. As Bo and Luke soon discover, things are still much the same in Hazzard. For the past couple of months, Cooter has been moonlighting at the Chickasaw Garage and getting hardly any sleep—and for a good reason. Boss Hogg has deliberately raised Cooter's mortgage to a balloon payment of $5,000 so Boss can have a reason to foreclose on Cooter's garage, because Boss wants to build a new shopping center in its place. Also, NASCAR driver Petey Willis (Donald May) has come out of retirement to prepare for the Atlanta 500. But Petey's car crashes during a practice run after Cooter worked on it and installed high-performance gas hoses in the engine. Petey's daughter Sarah Ann (Lori-Nan Engler) gets upset and blames Cooter, so a devastated Cooter decides to sell the Hazzard Garage to Boss Hogg and move to the mountains to become a recluse. Boss tells Rosco to take the Hazzard Garage's deed to Atlanta and record it. Bo and Luke figure out the cause of the crash: the pressure going through the fuel line burst a hole in the line, spraying gas all over the manifold. The Dukes are surprised that the manifold did not burn up. In an attempt to kill Petey, someone removed a high-performance fuel hose that Cooter installed and replaced it with a low-performance, store-bought fuel line, knowing it would blow and cause Petey to wreck. Sarah Ann tells Bo and Luke that Petey's backup driver, Joey Bryan (Chuck Wagner), is not happy about Petey driving in the Atlanta 500 because Joey himself wants to drive in the race. It was Joey who installed the low-performance fuel line in Petey's car. It turns out that Joey wanted Petey out of the way because he had bet on someone else to win the Atlanta 500 and stands a good chance of losing the bet unless Petey is out of the race. While Bo and Luke go after Joey, Jesse tells Cooter what is going on, and Daisy comes up with a plan to stop Rosco from recording the deed to the Hazzard Garage. Bo and Luke sign up as Big Brothers to Andy Slocum (P. R. Paul), a teenage orphan who steals the General Lee, some hubcaps, and other things. Bo and Luke try to point Andy in the right direction and help him stop stealing things—and then Andy stumbles upon a sack of Boss Hogg's dirty money in an abandoned mine near one of Jesse's abandoned moonshine stills. Andy finds himself on the run from Boss and crooked businessman Barney Benson (William Edward-Phipps), who want the money back. Boss pulls out all the stops to foreclose or buy all the land in Hazzard County so he and his new business partner, Lisa Sue "L. S." Pritchard (Randi Brooks), who is from Dallas, Texas, can develop "New Hazzard". When the Dukes lose the farm after Pritchard's goons keep them from making their mortgage payment, they investigate what Pritchard really wants the land for. When they find her plans to turn Hazzard County into a strip mine to mine coal, they have to convince Boss of it before Hazzard County becomes a big, empty hole. Bo and Luke have been overprotective towards Daisy ever since they returned to Hazzard, so Daisy, who is tired of being smothered, decides to move into the rooming house that her friend Sally Jo (Jo McDonnell) lives in. The Beaudrys, a moonshining family from a remote part of Tennessee, come into Hazzard to make a moonshine deal with Boss Hogg. After realizing the importance of family, Daisy decides to return to the Duke farm, but Daisy, along with Rosco's dog Flash, is kidnapped by the Beaudrys. The Beaudrys also take $20,000 belonging to Boss Hogg. Milo Beaudry (Richard Moll) wants a dog and a wife and wants Daisy to be his wife. Bo, Luke, Jesse, Rosco, and Boss set off to rescue Daisy and Flash. To rescue Daisy and Flash, Bo and Luke must take to the air in a pair of ultralights. When the so-called preacher (Dennis Fimple) arrives and Daisy is being forced at gunpoint to marry Milo, Bo and Luke show up to rescue Daisy and Flash. Lulu is frustrated over Boss Hogg constantly taking her for granted, so she walks out on him. Lulu is invited to stay on the Duke farm to sort out her emotions, but her stay is short-lived. She is kidnapped by Billy Ray (Chris Mulkey), Anna Lisa (Shanna Reed), and Eddie (Lewis Van Bergen), who demand that Boss pay a $100,000 ransom for her safe return. Billy Ray, Anna Lisa, and Eddie are making that demand because they are fed up with financial problems. Jesse alerts Bo, Luke, and Daisy about Lulu's disappearance (she had secretly tape-recorded the kidnapping), and the Dukes quickly offer to help Boss Hogg, who is genuinely devastated. However, he rebuffs them, particularly since the kidnappers have threatened to kill Lulu if the Dukes attempt a rescue. The ultimatum causes Bo and Luke (with some help from Cooter) to get creative in coming up with a plan to save Lulu. It leads to a confrontation at the Tri-County Amusement Park, which is set to be opened soon. Lulu helps apprehend the gang when she forces Anna Lisa into the getaway car and proceeds to sit on her and bounce up and down until Bo and Luke return with Eddie and Billy Ray. After a family picnic, the Dukes find a baby boy with a note in the General Lee. The note says for the Dukes to take care of the baby until the mother can safely pick him up. The baby's mother is Mary Lou Tompkins (Janeen Best), whose parents are the Dukes' old friends Bill and Bonnie Tompkins. Mary Lou is in a custody battle against baby Jamie's wealthy, snobby grandfather Emerson P. Craig (Peter Hobbs), who is from Savannah. Emerson wants to keep Jamie away from Mary Lou just because Mary Lou is a farmer's daughter and Mary Lou put Jamie in the General Lee to keep Jamie away from Emerson. A couple of years ago, Emerson's son Roger married Mary Lou without Emerson's approval and against his orders. Not long after Jamie was born, Roger passed away. Emerson did not approve of Mary Lou because, in his opinion, she used to work in one of his cotton mills and is a "nobody" because she was raised on a "grubby" farm. Emerson went to court and, with his high-priced attorney, had Mary Lou declared an unfit mother, and Emerson won custody of Jamie. It is too risky for the Dukes to keep Jamie at the Duke farm because Emerson has a pair of gun-carrying private investigators looking for Jamie. Daisy volunteers to go into hiding with Jamie at the abandoned Hazzard Sawmill building. Emerson's snobby attitude even angers Boss Hogg and Rosco, so Boss Hogg, Rosco, and Enos try to help the Dukes keep Jamie away from Emerson, and Boss Hogg and Jesse try to locate Judge Charles Druten (Ted Gehring), hoping that he can help. But because of a cut in the county budget, Rosco and Enos have to ride around on horses instead of in cars. Jesse and Boss Hogg locate Judge Druten and send him a message.

doc_name: List of The Dukes of Hazzard episodes
text: Years ago, Emerson's son Roger married Mary Lou without Emerson's approval and against his orders. Not long after Jamie was born, Roger died. Emerson did not approve of Mary Lou because, in his opinion, she was a "nobody" raised on a "grubby" farm and had previously worked in one of Emerson's cotton mills. Emerson went to court and, with his high-priced attorney, had Mary Lou declared an unfit mother, winning custody of Jamie. It is too risky for the Dukes to keep Jamie at the Duke farm because Emerson has a pair of gun-carrying private investigators searching for Jamie. Daisy volunteers to go into hiding with Jamie at the abandoned Hazzard Sawmill building. Emerson's snobby attitude even angers Boss Hogg and Rosco, so Boss Hogg, Rosco, and Enos try to help the Dukes keep Jamie away from Emerson, and Boss Hogg and Jesse attempt to locate Judge Charles Druten (Ted Gehring), hoping he can help. However, due to a cut in the county budget, Rosco and Enos must ride around on horses instead of in cars. Jesse and Boss Hogg locate Judge Druten and send Bo and Luke to pick him up. When Emerson and his private investigators close in on the Hazzard Sawmill building, one investigator accidentally sets fire to the surrounding woods by throwing down a lit cigar, forcing Bo and Luke, arriving with Judge Druten, to go into the fire to find Daisy and Jamie. After rescuing Daisy and Jamie from the fire, Jesse, Mary Lou, and Judge Druten help Emerson realize what a fool he has been, and he allows Mary Lou to have custody of Jamie. During a pursuit of the General Lee, another car runs Rosco off the road and into the Hazzard pond. Rosco climbs out uninjured, but the car's occupants kidnap him. Their leader is a man named Woody (James Best), who underwent plastic surgery to look exactly like Rosco. Bo and Luke see Rosco's car sink into the pond, but, as far as they know, Rosco is not surfacing as he normally does. When Bo and Luke turn around to check on Rosco and cannot find him, they fear the worst and assume he has drowned. The residents of Hazzard believe Rosco is dead. Later, at Rosco's supposed wake, everyone is overjoyed when they see "Rosco" stumbling down the street, but they do not realize it is actually Woody. Woody claims to be Rosco but makes enough mistakes to make everyone question the person they think is Rosco. Rosco's dog Flash is not fooled and will not go near the phony Rosco. When Bo and Luke take Woody to the hospital, still thinking he is Rosco, they are grabbed by Woody's accomplices Kelly (Clancy Brown) and Arnie (Jeffrey Josephson). What no one knows is that Woody, Kelly, and Arnie plan to rob an armored truck carrying $1,000,000 to the Hazzard Bank and frame Rosco for the robbery. Woody imprisons the Duke boys and the General Lee in their hideout (where the real Rosco is also being kept) so they cannot interfere with the robbery. It becomes a race against time to stop Woody and his accomplices from carrying out the robbery. Luke's long-lost biological brother Jud Kane (Randy Hamilton) arrives in Hazzard. Luke believed Jud was killed in a hospital fire as a baby, but it turns out Jud was rescued by a nurse who raised him as her own son. Jud is now a boxer known as Killer Kane and is being chased by Tex Tompkins (Christopher Stone), a crooked gambler who bet all his money on Jud's opponent and wanted Jud to throw the fight. Jud won after refusing to throw it, resulting in heavy losses for Tex. Now, Tex and his sidekick Charlie Burns (Phillip Clark) are out to kill Jud to send a message that no one is ever to cross Tex again, but Jesse, Bo, Luke, and Daisy will stop at nothing to keep Jud safe. Tex and Charlie trick Boss and Rosco into revealing Jud's whereabouts, then lock them in a holding cell to prevent interference. Luke later devises a plan to fool Tex by driving Jud's car and engaging in a road chase. But Luke is run off the road by Tex and Charlie and is taken to the Tri-County Hospital. Tex and Charlie, thinking they have succeeded in killing Jud, go to the Boar's Nest to celebrate, but overhear Enos telling Daisy that Luke has been injured. Knowing Jud is still alive, Tex and Charlie renew their pursuit, tracking Jud down at the Tri-County Hospital where they kidnap him, and Bo is unable to stop them. Bo tells Jesse, Luke, and Daisy what happened and then takes off after Tex and Charlie. Luke commandeers an ambulance and runs Tex and Charlie's car off the road and into a lake. The occupants are trapped inside as the car plunges to the bottom, and it is up to Bo to rescue Jud, Tex, and Charlie. When Bo and Luke are late for a probation appointment, Boss Hogg tells them he will let them off the hook if they coach Hazzard's pee wee basketball team, the Boar's Nest Bears. With Jesse's help, they convince 12-year-old Rod Moffet (Jason Lively), a talented basketball player shaken by the recent death of his father, to play for the Bears. Rod lives in Chickasaw County. Boss Hogg wants the Bears to win a championship game against the Chickasaw Chiefs, an undefeated team that Boss Hogg bet against, with Chickasaw County Commissioner A. C. Tate Jr. (Gailard Sartain), who is betting against the Bears. Tate and the Chiefs' head coach Ruel McBride (James Carroll Jordan) are willing to use any dirty trick to prevent Rod from playing. Tate even threatens to foreclose on the Moffet farm if Rod plays. After a talk with Bo and Luke, Rod decides not to give in to Tate. Bo and Luke are exasperated when they learn about the bet. Just before the game's opening tip-off, Tate presents a seemingly authentic birth certificate to the game administrator, Jesse, falsely claiming Rod is older than 12. While Luke is coaching the Bears, Bo and Daisy race to the Chickasaw County Courthouse to get the real birth certificate, but they must dodge Chickasaw County Sheriff Big Ed Little to get there. Pa Beaudry (J. S. Young) and his two sons Sledge (John Dennis Johnston) and Milo (Richard Moll) return to Hazzard to take one of Boss Hogg's moonshining stills after the Beaudrys' still blows up due to Milo's actions. To get Boss Hogg out of the way, the Beaudrys frame him for sabotaging Jesse's car during the Ridgerunner Old Timer's race when Jesse's car flips over. Jesse is not injured, but parts from his car are found in one of Boss Hogg's pockets, and Rosco puts Boss Hogg in jail while the Beaudrys take one of his stills. When Boss Hogg learns of the still theft, he tries to convince Rosco that the Beaudrys framed him to get him out of the way so they could take his still. Jesse believes Boss Hogg when he says he would never intentionally harm Jesse. The last time the Beaudrys were in Hazzard, they kidnapped Daisy and Flash and tried to force Daisy to marry Milo. Bo and Luke investigate and discover that Pa Beaudry slipped the car parts into Boss Hogg's pocket, leading to a confrontation with the Beaudrys on their property in a remote part of Tennessee. Terry Lee (Danny Cooksey), a six-year-old orphan who has become withdrawn after losing his parents in a car crash, is cared for by Ira Grant (Wally Taylor) at the orphanage. Bo and Luke help Terry Lee by getting him a basset hound from the pound. It turns out to be Maxine, the valuable purebred showdog that was kidnapped from wealthy John J. Hooper (Joe Dorsey) at a dog show, and the kidnappers, a man named B. B. (Billy Ray Sharkey) and his wife Mandy Jo (Jennifer Holmes), have demanded a $25,000 ransom. B. B. had worked for John for eight years before being fired. Maxine escaped and ended up in the pound when B. B. and Mandy Jo came to Hazzard. John and his wife (Toni Sawyer) have posted a $10,000 reward for Maxine's return. Boss Hogg, who wants the reward, learns Maxine is at the orphanage and, unaware of Terry Lee's feelings, takes her and holds her until John arrives. B. B. and Mandy Jo mistake Rosco's dog Flash for Maxine and, as a result, kidnap Flash. While everyone is looking for Flash, Boss Hogg remains hopeful about collecting the reward for Maxine. After everything is resolved, B. B. and Mandy Jo are found, Flash is rescued, and the Hoopers decide to adopt Terry Lee. Daisy and Lulu return from a shopping trip to New Orleans. At the airport, Lulu accidentally picks up a suitcase identical to her own, which contains a stolen $250,000 diamond necklace. When the thieves and their boss, Mr. Lipton (Robert Phalen), learn that Lulu and Daisy have the suitcase, they begin pursuing them, bent on retrieving the necklace by any means necessary. Boss Hogg wants the necklace to sell it to his crooked cousin, Big Dan Hogg (Marty Zagon), for $25,000—without realizing how valuable the necklace truly is. Bo, Luke, and Enos—later joined by Boss and Rosco—devise a plan to trap Lipton and his men and return the necklace to its owner, knowing that Lipton and his men have threatened to kill Daisy and Lulu if they fail to hand over the necklace or if any entrapment is detected. After returning from a Marine Corps reunion, Luke chases a woman who robbed a jewelry store in Capitol City, while at the same time, her identical twin sister is with Bo on the side of the road in a different part of the county, providing an alibi for the twins, Cindy (Randi Brough) and Sandy Ballou (Candi Brough). This causes a feud between Luke and Bo. Luke knows the woman he chased committed the robbery, and Bo refuses to believe Luke, thinking the woman in Capitol City is the same as the one on the road with Bo. The situation is resolved when Bo and Luke realize they are dealing with twins. In an effort to save money, Rosco and Enos have their patrol cars taken away by Boss Hogg, who gives them a pair of three-wheel ATVs to drive. While Enos was on the LAPD, he arrested and testified against hit man Frank Scanlon (Don Gordon). Now, Scanlon, who wears a different disguise for each job, has escaped from prison and arrived in Hazzard, determined to make Enos pay for putting him away. The Dukes help Enos capture Scanlon. Rosco's inattention allows Scanlon to escape from Hazzard jail, and Boss Hogg fires Enos for it. After Scanlon blows up Enos' empty car with a bomb, the Dukes and some friends set a trap to stop Scanlon before he can hurt Enos, but Scanlon turns the tables and kidnaps Daisy, believing the easiest way to get Enos is through Daisy. Scanlon demands that Enos give himself up alone or he will kill Daisy. The Dukes and everyone else in Hazzard set out to rescue Enos and Daisy and help Enos get his job back. Daisy, who has her pilot license, fills in for Hazzard County's crop duster, her boyfriend Joe Ward (Michael Crabtree), when Joe is injured. Boss Hogg has two crooks, Percy (Steven Williams) and Hector (Nick Benedict), secretly mix poisonous lye in the crop duster's pesticide mixer. As Boss had planned, Daisy kills Boss Hogg's crops so Boss can sue the Dukes for damages, hoping to win the Duke farm. However, Boss Hogg's scheme backfires when Percy and Hector form their own plan: they tell the county's farmers to pay a ransom or get lye dumped on their crops. The Dukes set out to stop Percy and Hector before Hazzard becomes a wasteland. 18-year-old Nancy Lou Nelson (Kim Richards) comes to Hazzard to see Cooter, and Nancy Lou turns out to be Cooter's long-lost biological daughter. Years ago, Cooter and local girl Beverly Hibbs ran away and got married. Back then, Cooter was still a wild man. Beverly's father had the marriage annulled, but not before Beverly became pregnant. Because of Cooter's wild side, Beverly and Cooter agreed it would be better if she raised Nancy Lou alone. Now, Cooter tries to be respectable, but seems unable to avoid brushes with strangers named Collins (David Gale) and Buck Morgan (Jack Yates), who lead a group planning to dump toxic waste in Hazzard County. Nancy Lou begins to believe Beverly was right about Cooter and plans to leave town. Bo, Luke, and Cooter set out to stop Collins and Morgan, and the Dukes try to help Cooter redeem his image in Nancy Lou's eyes. When Boss Hogg learns what Collins and Morgan are up to, he makes it clear he does not want toxic waste in Hazzard County. Private investigator Harry Bobo (Frank Birney) comes to Hazzard with a photo of heiress Vivian Stewart, the long-lost granddaughter of wealthy industrialist Carter Stewart (Lyle Talbot)—who is offering a $200,000 reward to anyone who finds Vivian. It turns out Vivian looks exactly like Daisy, so Boss Hogg, who wants the reward money, has Professor Crandall (Walker Edmiston) hypnotize Daisy into thinking she is Vivian. Boss Hogg tricks Harry into thinking Daisy is Vivian, and they visit Carter. But Vivian's cousins Alan Fairchild (Greg Michaels) and Vonnie Fairchild (Nancy Hinman), who would inherit Vivian's estate if she is killed, are out to kill Daisy because they also believe Daisy is Vivian. Bo and Luke chase armored truck robbers Phil (Charles Cyphers) and Lenny (Charles H. Hyman) through Chickasaw County, and Sheriff Ed Little mistakes the Dukes for the robbers. The only eyewitness who can clear Bo and Luke is their old friend, local artist Artie Bender (James Cavan)—but Boss Hogg has just hidden Artie away and declared him legally dead so Boss can sell Artie's paintings to an art dealer at inflated prices. Chickasaw County Sheriff "Big Ed" Little continues to pursue Bo and Luke after they escape from jail, as they try to unravel the mystery of whether Artie is really dead. Country music star Candy Dix (Roberta Leighton), a woman Luke courted before he enlisted in the Marines, comes to Hazzard to do a concert at the Boar's Nest and see Luke for the first time in seven years. As they try to rekindle their romance, Luke finds that Candy has a lot on her mind. Her current boyfriend and manager, Eddie Lee Memphis (Jeff Osterhage), is with her.
