text: Through Chickasaw County, Sheriff Ed Little mistakes the Dukes for the robbers. The only eyewitness who can clear Bo and Luke is their old friend, local artist Artie Bender (James Cavan), but Boss Hogg has hidden Artie away and declared him legally dead so Boss can sell Artie's paintings to an art dealer at inflated prices. Chickasaw County Sheriff "Big Ed" Little continues to pursue Bo and Luke after they escape from jail, as they try to unravel the mystery of whether Artie is really dead. Country music star Candy Dix (Roberta Leighton), a woman Luke courted before he enlisted in the Marines, comes to Hazzard to do a concert at the Boar's Nest and see Luke for the first time in seven years. As they try to rekindle their romance, Luke finds Candy has a lot on her mind; her current boyfriend and manager, Eddie Lee Memphis (Jeff Osterhage), has been ill-tempered and abusive toward her, because Memphis owes a gambling debt to bookie Mr. Starkey (Ritch Brinkley), who threatens to kill him if the debt is not paid. Memphis is terrified, and the Dukes must protect Candy from Memphis and his accomplice Hoby Willis (Ned Bellamy), who are out to kill her so Memphis can use her $75,000 life insurance policy to pay off the debt. While protecting Candy, Memphis tries to prevent interference by visiting Boss Hogg and asking that Luke be arrested for kidnapping. Bo and Luke are offered a chance to return to the NASCAR circuit, racing for Mary Beth Carver (Lydia Cornell), the daughter of crime boss J. J. Carver (Ramon Bieri). Mary Beth is not involved in Carver's operations. Bo and Luke decline, vowing to uphold a promise they made to Jesse that they would never again leave the farm to race. A Federal Agent named Walden (Herbert Jefferson, Jr.) later approaches Bo and Luke, offering a healthy cash sum for them to work undercover as race car drivers for Mary Beth, since J. J. Carver is involved in a gambling racket involving murder, robbery, and illegal gambling. The offer is too good to pass up, and Bo and Luke agree to work for Walden, who tells them they cannot tell Jesse and Daisy what they are doing, leaving clueless Daisy angry. Daisy berates Bo and Luke for leaving her and Jesse to return to racing after their promise, even slapping Bo. Bo and Luke begin to infiltrate J. J. Carver's organization, compiling evidence to bring him to justice. The Tri-Counties 150 is underway at a track in Capitol City, and Bo is driving Carver's race car, but their cover is blown—thanks to Boss Hogg and Rosco, who think Bo and Luke are making gambling deals. After tying up Luke, Boss, and Rosco, Carver (Ramon Bieri) sends his henchman Jo Jo (Mike Moroff) to the track to kill Bo as soon as he crosses the finish line. When Jesse and Daisy show up at the track, Bo, unaware he is putting Daisy's life in danger, has Daisy secretly take his place in the race so he can go to Carver's home and help Luke, Boss, and Rosco recover the evidence. Once Carver is brought down and Bo and Luke are allowed to tell Daisy and Jesse what they were doing, Daisy realizes she made a mistake in getting angry and apologizes to them. Boss Hogg's nephew Dewey Hogg (Robert Morse), who is Hughie Hogg's older brother, returns to Hazzard for the first time in seven years and says he is dying from a rare and lethal sleeping disorder. Dewey convinces Boss that he wants to build the Dewey Hogg Memorial Clinic as his legacy, if Boss will put up $50,000 and get the town to contribute another $50,000. The plan works, and Dewey and Boss get Jesse to guard the money, which then goes missing, and Dewey frames Jesse for the scam. Luke and Daisy discover Dewey is faking his illness, and the Dukes devise a plan to get him to lead them to the money. Luke pretends to order a very expensive stomach pump to save his life, and Dewey, in distress, rushes to the bank to find the money to pay for it. It is revealed that Dewey had transferred the money into a different safety deposit box. However, Luke's plan goes sour when Boss and Rosco expose their scheme. Dewey escapes, and the Dukes must follow him in a long car chase. Dewey and his nurse assistant are stopped and made to march out of Hazzard in disgrace without the money. Daisy will play a nurse in a play at the church and carries her notes in a black book. Nervous Norman Willis (Mike Genovese), a neurotic crime boss, comes to Hazzard County to collect a debt from Boss Hogg. While Norman's limo is in front of the General Lee, the car backfires, and Norman, living up to his nickname, mistakes it for a gunshot. A scared Norman, thinking he is having a heart attack, has his driver Jake (Kaz Garas) rush him into town. In town, Norman and Jake see Daisy wearing a nurse uniform and do not realize she is practicing for the play. Jake gets Daisy's attention, and Daisy comes to help Norman. Norman puts his little black book next to him on the back seat. Daisy puts down her black book, which is identical to Norman's. Jake and Norman decide to go to the local hospital, but first, Daisy grabs her rehearsal notes—or so she thinks. She actually grabs Norman's black book, which contains information on all of his crooked operations. When Norman discovers he has the wrong book, he is terrified Daisy has the information that could put him in prison. He and Jake go out hunting for Daisy, intending to get the book and kill her to prevent her from revealing their activities. Bo, Luke, and Jesse decide to hide Daisy in Enos's house while they look for Norman and Jake. Norman tells Boss Hogg that his debt will be cleared if he helps Norman find Daisy. Enos unwittingly lets Daisy's location slip to Rosco, and Rosco and Boss tell Willis and Jake where to find her, promising she will be unharmed. Boss Hogg, who does not condone violence, is unaware Norman plans to have Jake kill Daisy. Norman and Jake kidnap Daisy from Enos's house, and it is up to the Dukes, Cooter, and Enos to rescue her. Recently, the cash flow from Boss Hogg's scams has slowed to a trickle. In Boss's opinion, things would be better if he could get Enos out of the way and hire a deputy who would look the other way and keep the Dukes out of the way. To achieve this, Boss promotes Enos to Hazzard Commissioner of Records and hires Billy Joe Coogan (Michael Alldredge), from Cedar City, as the tough new deputy, who proves to be an unexpected challenge for the Dukes. What Boss does not know is that Coogan is hatching a crooked plan with Eddie Hollis (Joseph Whipp). Coogan and Hollis have helped Boss Hogg with scams before, but now there is more than $150,000 that Boss skimmed from the county over the past years, and he placed it in a hidden account. Coogan learns about it when he sees Boss's secret ledger, and Coogan and Hollis demand that Boss give up the money or the spillway at the Hazzard dam will be opened as far as it will go. If the spillway is set wide open for long enough, all of Hazzard will be flooded under about 10 feet of water, and every farm in Hazzard County will be washed out. The Dukes are in a race against time to stop Coogan and Hollis and help Enos get his deputy job back. Boss Hogg is in a stew after discovering that Lulu is going to cash in the $100,000 in bonds that Boss already cashed in on and replaced with fake bonds. Boss must get rid of the fake bonds. The problem is, Lulu has changed the combination of the safe that she and Boss Hogg keep at home. Boss hires Madame Delilah (Leslie Easterbrook) and Three Pack (Tommy Madden), a pair of fortune-teller con artists, to get the safe combination from Lulu and get rid of the fake bonds. But complications arise because Madame Delilah and Three Pack have robbed the Boar's Nest. Rosco and Boss Hogg, unaware that Madame Delilah and Three Pack are the robbers, accuse Daisy of the robbery. Luke and Jesse must hide Daisy from Rosco. Daisy and Luke discover the truth about Madame Delilah and Three Pack. They have been robbing Hazzard blind with their scams. Boss Hogg is angry at their victimization of Lulu and demands that Madame Delilah and Three Pack be put in jail. Luke and Daisy try to find Madame Delilah and Three Pack and prove Daisy's innocence. Recurring guest: Peggy Rea as Lulu Coltrane Hogg. Jonas Jones (Hal Williams) rescued Cooter from a fire in Oklahoma 10 years ago, and they have been friends ever since. An auto parts supply distribution firm, scheduled to deliver a shipment of parts for Boss Hogg, is a front for a hijacking and theft ring led by John Harris (George McDaniel). When Jonas is framed for a hijacking by Harris's crew, Cooter takes the rap for Jonas to stop Harris from framing him. This is much to Boss and Rosco's delight, since Cooter unwittingly implicates Bo and Luke as accessories. With Jonas in hiding, Bo and Luke help Cooter escape from jail. While Jesse and Daisy try to infiltrate Harris's distribution firm, Luke goes undercover as a driver for their operation to set a trap for the hijackers, but when Rosco and Boss show up to arrest Bo and Cooter, they are forced to take drastic action. The Dukes are celebrating the anniversary of the day they got the General Lee eight years ago in 1976, and we see the story of how they got it. Eight years ago, Luke was just out of the Marines, and Bo was just out of high school. Two jewel thieves named Ginny (Janie Fricke) and Rick (Sam Melville) hid $50,000 worth of gold dust under the dashboard of a black Dodge Charger. The car was wrecked and taken to a junkyard. Bo and Luke were searching for a race car to compete in a local race with a $10,000 prize. Their search led them to the black Dodge Charger. The Dukes bought the car and took it to Cooter's garage to soup it up and paint it its current color, orange—the only color Cooter had at his garage at the time. It was Jesse's idea to name it the General Lee. The number 01, as Bo explained, means "From here on out, it's number one all the way." Ginny and Rick go after the Dukes to get the gold dust, but the Dukes manage to stop them, win the race, and keep the General Lee. After six seasons of complaining in song that they "keep showing my hands and not my face on TV," Waylon Jennings finally appears on The Dukes of Hazzard, on camera. An old friend of the Duke family, Waylon brings his tour bus and traveling museum to Hazzard County. Years ago, before his first professional gig, someone stole Waylon Jennings's guitar. With no money to replace it, he would have missed his opportunity, but then a stranger loaned him the money to replace it. That stranger was Jesse Duke. They have been friends ever since. Waylon enters Hazzard, traveling in a very valuable mobile country music history museum to use as a charity exhibit. This museum, considering its value, is a desirable item for a thief. Boss Hogg is always willing to do almost anything for money. Boss hires two crooks named Buddy (Stephen Lee) and Jeb (Terrence Evans) to steal the museum and hold it for ransom. Bo, Luke, and Daisy are on their way to an old-fashioned hay ride. Meanwhile, a truck carrying an experimental genetic drug accidentally drops a vial of it into the Hazzard pond. Shortly after, the Dukes must stop at the pond to get water for the General Lee's radiator, since it has overheated. While filling a jug of water from the lake, Luke also takes a small drink. He does not realize he is drinking water contaminated by the genetic drug. Luke begins to experience a severe personality change. He becomes obnoxious and turns on Bo. When they get to the hay ride, Luke insults Enos and says he now sees that Hazzard is just a joke of a town. When all the Dukes are back at the farm, Luke continues to insult his family. He forgoes the ceremony of saying grace and insults Uncle Jesse's cooking. For Bo, this is the last straw, and he wants to have it out with Luke. Jesse asks Bo to hold back. Luke takes off in the General. Out of respect for Jesse's wishes, Bo agrees to go look for the dramatically changed Luke. Luke, now under the full influence of the drug, goes on a rampage, even running Bo off the road. Luke is observed by Hurley (Alan Autry) and Ben (Greg Finley), two men planning to rob the Hazzard Bank, and they are looking for a good getaway driver. Luke, in his current frame of mind, agrees to help them for a cut of the money. Soon, Boss Hogg becomes aware of Hurley and Ben's plans to rob his bank and begins to devise his own plan to catch Hurley, Ben, and especially Luke in the act. Meanwhile, the remaining Dukes discover the empty genetic drug vial at the lake and go to the research company in Atlanta to find out more information, hoping to save Luke from its effects. Dr. Debbie Davis (Lori Hallier) tells them the drug will not wear off until 11:00 AM the following morning. The Dukes hurry back to Hazzard to try to prevent Luke from getting himself into trouble. However, they arrive too late. Luke has already done the robbery with Hurley and Ben, and he has been videotaped by Boss's surveillance cameras. It is up to Uncle Jesse and Daisy to catch up to Rosco and get the tape from him before he delivers it to the authorities. Rosco is unwilling to listen to their story, but Rosco's dog Flash chews the tape up. Bo and Enos find Hurley and Ben. Bo has it out with Luke. During the fight, the drug wears off, and Luke is his old self again. Luke apologizes to everyone he insulted while under the influence of the drug, and everyone is forgiving. A computer technician named Rance (Ray Colbert) is fired from his job shortly after completing work on a contract. He and a co-worker named Marv (William Allen Young) get revenge against their former employer by stealing a cache of electronics to sell on the black market, then stealing them back for ransom. text: During the fight, the drug wears off, and Luke is his old self again. Luke apologizes to everyone he had insulted while under the influence, and everyone forgives him. A computer technician named Rance (Ray Colbert) is fired shortly after completing work on a contract. He and his co-worker Marv (William Allen Young) get revenge by stealing a cache of electronics to sell on the black market and later stealing them back for ransom. One of the stolen items is an advanced robot named Bobby Joe (Robert Shields). Bo and Luke, who previously had a conflict with Rance and Marv, become suspicious and investigate their van. Rosco catches the Duke boys inside the van but bungles the arrest. The robot easily apprehends the Dukes. Boss Hogg is impressed, buys the robot, and promotes Bobby Joe to Hazzard County Sheriff. Hogg is unaware that Marv and Rance plan to use Bobby Joe to rob the Hazzard Bank. The Dukes become suspicious and begin investigating, eventually finding the crooks' hideout and their ransom note to the electronics company, proving Bobby Joe was stolen. When Marv and Rance discover the Dukes have been snooping, they capture them and tie them up before heading to rob the bank. After loading all the loot into their truck, they have Bobby Joe hold Rosco at the scene to make it appear as if Rosco robbed the bank. When Boss Hogg arrives, he is angry at Rosco until the Dukes explain everything about Marv and Rance. The Dukes flee in the General, followed by Rosco and Enos, to find Marv and Rance. Bo and Luke stop Marv and Rance's truck and grab them. Rosco and Enos arrive just in time to capture Marv and Rance and recover the stolen money. Rosco is now a proud sheriff once again. A senator is visiting Hazzard to inspect law enforcement, and Boss Hogg frames the Dukes by convincing them that Daisy won prizes, including a fur coat and a diamond necklace, at the Capitol City Department Store as the 1,000,000th customer—though the prizes were stolen from Boss Hogg's own robbery. Just as Hogg plans to send the Dukes to prison, he takes a blow to the head and wakes up with amnesia. He suddenly becomes a nice guy and double-crosses his partners Stoney (John Matuszak) and Zack (Jan Eddy), who want to silence him. While a Hollywood production company is filming in Hazzard, star Brock Curtis (Barry Van Dyke) loses brake control in his car and is saved by the Dukes. The producers offer the Dukes a part in the movie. The Dukes, with Boss and Rosco, travel to Hollywood. In Hollywood, Boss and Rosco try to get into a movie, but Flash catches the attention of a talent agent. The Dukes discover that Brock's near-accident was no accident—producer Jason Dillard (Brett Halsey), who is facing severe financial problems, has taken out a $5,000,000 life insurance policy on Brock and has arranged for Blake (Frank Annese) to kill him to collect the money. The Dukes must stop Dillard and Blake. Boss Hogg's arch-enemy, Colonel Cassius B. Claybourne (Morgan Woodward), commissioner of Osage County, plans to take over Hazzard County. He arrests Bo and Luke while they pass through Osage County and puts them on the chain gang, where they are harassed by guards led by Captain Slater (Brion James). With public pressure mounting, Boss and Rosco give in to Claybourne's demand to surrender Boss's moonshine contracts in exchange for Bo and Luke's freedom. When they go to Osage County to retrieve Bo and Luke, Claybourne arrests them and places them on the road gang along with Bo and Luke. Claybourne exploits Boss's love for high-calorie food to extort him, eventually forcing him to give up most of Hazzard County. Bo, Luke, and Daisy, along with Jesse and General Lee, must break everyone out and reclaim Hazzard from Claybourne and his sheriff, R. P. "Droopy" Cathcarte (Claude Earl Jones). After inheriting his grandfather's estate, Boss Hogg finds a letter from Jesse's great-great-grandfather Jeremiah Duke stating that Jeremiah signed the Duke farm over to Boss Hogg's great-great-grandfather Thaddeus B. Hogg in 1872, when Hazzard was known as Sleepy City. Boss evicts the Dukes from the farm, but before leaving, they examine Jeremiah's diary, which reveals that Thaddeus Hogg pressured Jeremiah to sell the farm. Bo, Luke, and Daisy's great-grandparents—Joe Duke, Hank Duke, and Dixie Duke—came to help Jeremiah and faced Hogg's hired men: Frank James (Nick Benedict) and Jesse James (Paul Koslo). When they could not scare off the Dukes, Hogg framed Hank for horse rustling and traded Hank's freedom for the farm. Thinking he had won, Hogg headed to town just as the James boys robbed his safe, capturing him and Rufus Z. Coltrane, Rosco's great-great-grandfather, and fleeing to the hills. The Dukes of old may have saved the day then, and this history may help the present-day Dukes keep the farm from Boss Hogg. Cale Yarborough visits Hazzard to see Robbie (Chad Sheets), an orphan about to undergo surgery at Tri-County Hospital. Eddie Scoggins (Al White) and Elmo Smith (Dennis Haskins), who robbed the Capitol City Bank and bought a hideout from Boss Hogg, frame Bo, Luke, and Cale for the robbery. A train is coming through Hazzard County with a box car containing over $3,000,000 in valuables. Boss Hogg hires three men—Burke (Wayne Grace), Carney (Steve James), and Perry (Ted Markland)—and masterminds a plan to knock the boxcar off the train using a remotely controlled car. When that car is wrecked, Burke, Carney, and Perry steal the General Lee instead. Using the General Lee would implicate Bo and Luke, so when Bo and Luke search for it, they are captured, gagged, and planned to be killed—something Boss would never approve of. Jesse and Daisy must find Bo and Luke and help them. Boss is appalled by the plan to kill Bo and Luke, so he, Rosco, and Enos join in to stop it. Escaped convict and former Marine Lee Benson (Judson Scott) and his accomplice Brad Hixx (Robert Gray) go to Hazzard to settle a score with Luke. While in the Marines, Luke was a sergeant and Benson had robbed his best friend's foot locker, which Luke discovered and had Benson imprisoned for several years. Now, Benson wants Luke to pay for that. As part of his plan, Benson orders Bo and Luke to drive them out of state in the General Lee at gunpoint, without revealing anything is wrong when approached by authorities. Chickasaw County Sheriff Big Ed Little (Don Pedro Colley), tracking Benson and Hixx, assumes the Dukes are helping them. To avoid detection, Benson and Hixx force Bo and Luke to drive through a forest fire. When Sheriff Little locks everyone except Enos in a holding cell, Bo and Luke rely on Enos' help and their own wits to stop Benson and Hixx. A group of armored car robbers—Kate (Karen Lamm), Taylor (Bob Hastings), Budge (Chip Heller), and Cleary (Michael Prokopuk)—steal an armored car by lifting it with a helicopter, carrying Boss' uninsured bank money. The Dukes are blamed for the theft. When Bo and Luke are arrested, the robbers strike again. Knowing the Dukes are innocent, Boss and Rosco allow them to escape so they can pursue the hijackers. The robbers then kidnap Daisy. Bo, Luke, Jesse, Enos, Boss, and Rosco team up to rescue Daisy. Bo and Luke take to the air to locate the gang's hideout. Boss Hogg's great-uncle Silas Hogg has died and left $100,000 to charity at the discretion of the executor, Jesse. Boss, wanting the money, tries every trick to become executor. At Silas' farm, the Dukes, with the help of a ventriloquist and special effects wizard named Mr. Winkle (Bill McLean), set up gadgets to make it appear that Silas is haunting Boss, causing him to give up his plan. Boss's attorney, Larson (Jason Evers), tries to obtain the money. Hughie Hogg (Jeff Altman) returns to Hazzard with a plan to cheat Boss out of everything. With the help of Trixie (Katherine "Kitty" Moffat), Hughie makes Boss believe there is a genie in a magic lamp that grants untold wealth and a way to get rid of Bo and Luke. The Dukes must stop Hughie before Bo and Luke end up in prison, leaving Boss and Rosco with only a worthless lamp. There have been recent UFO sightings in Hazzard County, and Bo and Luke initially think people are crazy until an alien (Felix Silla) hides in the General Lee and returns to the Duke farm. Boss wants to use the visitor as a tourist attraction. At the same time, thieves Mickey Larsen (Dennis Burkley) and Buck Simmons (Britt Leach) are casing Hazzard for a planned bank robbery. Two crooks, Slade (Anthony De Longis) and Jerry (Scott Lincoln), force an unwilling Enos to hand over a bank transfer shipment. Daisy sees Enos with the money but does not see Slade and Jerry, who threaten to shoot her if Enos does not comply. Slade and Jerry escape. Because Daisy only sees Enos getting the money, the state's Deputy Attorney General (Michael Fairman) jails Enos for robbery. Daisy cannot refuse to testify against Enos or face contempt. Knowing Enos would never rob a bank, Daisy proposes marriage to him, as a wife cannot be legally forced to testify against her husband. Slade and Jerry try to stop the marriage because it would expose their frame-up. To clear Enos' name, Bo and Luke search for Slade and Jerry. Lulu Hogg stages her annual charity talent contest at the Boar's Nest. Rosco performs a magic act and names Boss Hogg as his assistant. Boss is annoyed because it conflicts with a scheduled business appointment. Knowing Lulu would walk out on him if he refuses, Boss agrees to participate. He schemes to use the "disappearance" to drive into town for his appointment. However, the disappearance works too well. Paroled convict Floyd Malone (Kevin Peter Hall) and his brother Bubba (Ji-Tu Cumbuka) want to make Boss pay for testifying against Floyd in a hijacking case three years ago. They kidnap Boss outside the Boar's Nest—unknown to Rosco, the Dukes, or others inside. After convincing Lulu that Boss's disappearance may have been foul play, Bo and Luke search for the Malones, who demand $1,000,000 or Boss will be killed. The Dukes struggle to convince grief-stricken Rosco that his magic was not responsible. Bo and Luke hatch a plan to rescue Boss. Once Boss is freed and the Malones are arrested, Bo and Luke convince Boss to complete the second half of Rosco's magic trick. Boss still refuses until he sees an emotional Rosco recalling their shared memories and how Boss was the only one who stood by him. Boss "reappears" on cue when Rosco performs the trick one last time. An overjoyed Rosco is happy to see Boss again.
